title: Command contract
body: BxCachy command contract (A5 draft, v3) Target (2026-11-09): Hyprland + Noctalia on CachyOS, KDE kept side by side; see plan.md section 19. setup is the headline command. Status: proposal, no code written. Note 2026-11-09: the legacy tree in artifacts/legacy/original/ is the real v0.10.0 source. It is kept as is and never copied, backed up or modified. Decisions here are inputs to M0 hardening (tasks 1.2 to 1.5) and M1 catalog work. Legacy v0.10.0 is a feature reference only ( artifacts/legacy/original/ ). 1. Grammar bxcachy <group> <verb> [args...] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] [--quiet] Groups mirror the legacy dispatcher so users keep their muscle memory: setup apps app-manager catalog profile base extras dev web podman ai vector db db-center vm network cloud cloud-center cloud-services files quicklook dictation integrations desktop desktop-keys mac-keys omarchy-base layout themes icons runner menu shortcuts system config first-run doctor setup . Global verbs on every group: plan (read-only), status (read-only), doctor (read-only checks), help . Mutating verbs: install , apply , remove , restore , enable , disable . All require --yes . Existing flat commands ( install , optional-install , profile-install , package-status , package-source , ...) stay as aliases until the grouped form ships, then print a deprecation note. Unknown flags, duplicate flags, empty arguments and extra positionals are usage errors (exit 2). Nothing runs. Note from M0 history: BoxLang CLIGetArgs() puts flags in args.options , not args.positionals . The parser is one shared function, tested once. 2. Mutation rules (apply to every mutating verb) No --yes : print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 2. --dry-run with --yes : print the exact plan, change nothing, exit 0. Preflight everything before the first mutation. A preflight failure means zero changes. Never escalate privilege silently. sudo is only called for pacman steps shown in the plan. Never run AUR builds as root (exit 4). Every config file touched goes through the config service (backup, atomic replace, journal). No direct writes. Output lists succeeded and failed items separately. No rollback is promised across pacman and yay. External installer scripts (bvm, mvm, toolchain node 's nvm, catalog source: script ) are downloaded to a temp file, their url and sha256 are printed, and they run as the normal user (never root) with no confirmation gate and no flag: the typed EXECUTE and --allow-external-scripts were removed on 2026-11-10 (owner: running them is the point of the command). Decision 2026-11-09: no checksum pinning for these scripts. Subprocesses are launched with argument arrays, never through a shell string. 3. Exit codes Code Meaning Example 0 Success or no-op already installed, or --dry-run 1 Check negative package-status says missing 2 Usage error or missing confirmation no --yes , unknown flag 3 Timeout, or item unavailable pacman lookup timed out, package not in any repo 4 Precondition failed root with AUR, not Arch, Java missing, not KDE where required 5 Official (pacman) phase failed 6 AUR (yay) phase failed 7 Partial success some items done, some failed; --json lists both 8 Config conflict drift detected, symlink or special file at target, concurrent run lock 9 Internal error bug, unexpected exception Codes 0 to 6 match what the native CLI returns today (2, 3, 4, 5, 6 are already used). 1 is already used for check-negative. 7 to 9 are new. Codes are frozen once published and covered by a contract snapshot test. 4. --json One JSON object on stdout, nothing else on stdout. Human text goes to stderr. { "schema": 1, "command": "profile install", "version": "0.11.0-dev", "ok": false, "exit": 7, "dry_run": false, "plan": [{"id": "jq", "source": "pacman", "action": "install"}], "done": [{"id": "jq", "source": "pacman"}], "failed": [{"id": "x", "source": "aur", "reason": "yay exited 1"}], "skipped": [{"id": "git", "reason": "already installed"}], "warnings": [] } Read-only commands use the same envelope with a data field. 5. Catalog (single source of truth) Decision already made: import legacy catalog/apps.json (482 entries) as canonical, keeping its 61 default flags. It replaces the hardcoded lists in src/bxcachy.bxs and scripts/package-manager.sh . Entry schema (legacy fields kept, new fields marked): Field Notes id , name , kind ( desktop tui web ), category , description as legacy source ( pacman aur pkgbuild script manual web ), target package name, or URL for web and script pkgbuild source: repo , path , ref Build with makepkg as the normal user from a PKGBUILD in a public git repo, pinned to a full 40-character commit ( catalog check rejects anything else), then install the result with pacman. Used for Omarchy 4.5 apps ( omacom/omarchy-pkgs ). The PKGBUILD is shown before it is built. check (for script ) argv array that exits 0 when installed, for example ["command","-v","pi"] default base tier flag source_status , source_confirmed legacy provenance flags, kept profiles (new) list of profile ids deps (new) other catalog ids check (new) optional post-install check, argv array verified_on (new) date the target was confirmed against real repos Findings from the legacy data (decisions recorded 2026-11-09): Unverified sources. 176 entries are source: manual (95 tui, 81 desktop). Their package names are unverified. Proposal: a CI job that checks every pacman / aur target against real repos (Arch container, AUR RPC) and fails on unknown names. manual entries stay installable only by explicit user action. Default list mismatch. 61 flagged default (29 pacman, 18 aur, 14 web). app-profile.json base lists 46. 20 defaults are not in that base list (for example ark dolphin dolphin-plugins kio-extras rclone fuse3 sshfs nfs-utils cifs-utils podman-desktop tabby beekeeper-studio google-docs google-sheets google-slides kompare filelight ffmpegthumbs kdegraphics-thumbnailers kimageformats ). 5 base entries are not flagged default ( dbeaver filezilla krdc podman-tui rustdesk ). The 61 flags win. The 5 dropped base entries are dbeaver (pacman), filezilla (pacman), krdc (pacman), rustdesk (aur) and podman-tui (manual). Pending: keep them as curated (not default), or re-flag any as default. Browsers. brave is aur ( brave-bin ) and default. A fresh default install therefore needs yay on day one. Decision: bootstrap installs yay only if it is not already present. Preserve list. Legacy preserve (CachyOS, KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Noctalia, existing user configs) becomes enforced rules, not just text. Named profiles keep the existing four ( core jvm containers terminal ) and are expressed as catalog profiles tags. Later profiles ( web backend ai ops desktop full ) are added only after package names are verified. Ship vs embed (pending confirmation): the default catalog is embedded in the binary at build time, so there is one file to ship and it always matches the code. An optional ~/.config/bxcachy/catalog.json adds entries or sets default / profiles on existing ids. It is validated against the same schema and can never delete or replace an embedded entry's target , so a bad override cannot redirect an install. 6. State and config layout ~/.config/bxcachy/ same root as legacy bxcachy.json global settings catalog.json optional user additions (merge-only) ai.json menu.json shortcuts.json ... one file per feature, as legacy ~/.local/state/bxcachy/ journal/ one record per apply: files, hashes, backup paths backups/ backups, indexed by the journal lock single-writer lock config list|diff|apply|restore work from the journal, so restore needs only an id. Retention default: keep the last 20 per file. Open: this applies to the user's config files that BxCachy writes, not to the legacy source tree. 7. Test contract A snapshot test freezes bxcachy help , the exit-code table and the --json schema. Every mutating verb needs these cases: success, no-op, invalid input, dependency failure, privilege rejection, partial failure, recovery. Real-system cases run in tests/arch/ (non-root, real pacman). Cases needing KDE, Wayland or hardware are marked manual and tracked in the acceptance log. 8. Catalog check, validation and reporting bxcachy catalog check [--json] [--online] plus a CI job that runs it in the Arch container. Offline validation (always, no network): schema version; unique ids; enums for kind / source ; web targets are https with no credentials or control characters; package targets match ^[a-zA-Z0-9@._+-]+$ ; default entries have a non- manual source; profiles and deps reference existing ids; no dependency cycles. Online verification ( --online , CI): every pacman target must resolve with pacman -Si (or -Sg for groups); every aur target must resolve through the AUR RPC ( /rpc/v5/info ); manual targets are probed against both and reported as promotable. Results are stored per entry as verified_on and a status: ok , moved (listed source is wrong but another source has it), missing , unverified . Reporting: a table by status and source for the console, --json for tools, and a markdown report in the CI step summary and artifact. Policy: missing entries with default: true fail CI; missing non-default entries are warnings listed in the report; moved entries are warnings with the suggested fix. First measurement (2026-11-09, stock Arch core/extra only, so CachyOS repos and multilib are not covered): Check Result pacman targets (118) 111 resolve, 7 do not: 5 exist in AUR ( git-cola insomnia localsend ulauncher wlogout ), 2 found nowhere ( intellij-idea-community-edition , swww ) aur targets (64) 40 resolve in AUR, 11 are now official ( doggo impala nwg-dock-hyprland opencode podman-desktop rio spotify-launcher superfile television warehouse zenmap ), 13 found nowhere ( beeper ctop dbgate espanso grokbot herder inshellisense notion-desktop pi-agent tmog todoist upnote zap-whatsapp ) manual targets (176) 93 are official packages today (promotable, for example jq ripgrep-all tmux kitty starship terraform kubectl ), 83 are not The check must also run against the CachyOS repos on a real CachyOS machine before any missing entry is removed. 9. Open questions The 5 dropped base entries: keep as curated, or re-flag any as default? Catalog embed with merge-only user override: confirmed? Hyprland features (layout, runner, shortcuts, menus) are now in scope, not deferred. 10. Implemented so far (2026-11-09) config list|diff|apply|restore|history (section 6 design; lock is a file created with fileWriteExclusive , temp files and journal records are created exclusive with their mode). Global flag check and the --json envelope (sections 1 and 4) for the read-only commands. catalog list|show|groups|check|version : the catalog is schema 3 ( catalog/README.md ) and is embedded in the binary by bootstrap/gen-catalog.sh (CI fails if src/bxcachy.bxs is stale). Filters use the --name=value form ( --tier=default --group=infra ), because MatchBox CLIGetArgs takes --name value as a flag plus a positional. catalog check is offline: errors exit 1, warnings (unpinned pkgbuild refs, default entries without a package) do not. The user override file is deliberately last (extensibility phase). 11. Package commands on the catalog (B2, decided 2026-11-09) Applies to plan , install-plan , install , optional-* , profile-* , package-status , package-source . All read the embedded catalog (schema 3). Hardcoded lists in Main.bx go away. Selection bxcachy install # tier default bxcachy install ID [ID...] # exactly these apps bxcachy install --profile=NAME # a profile bxcachy install --optional # default tier plus optional tier Naming an app is enough. There is no --aur flag : anything in the catalog installs from its source ( pacman , aur , pkgbuild , web ). Unknown id: usage error (exit 2), nothing runs. Skip reasons: optional (not selected), wrong_shell and unresolved (catalog has no installable source yet; a named unresolved app is reported failed , exit 3). Already installed apps are skipped with reason installed . Section 2 still applies: no --yes prints the plan and exits 2; --dry-run --yes prints it and exits 0. AUR and pkgbuild builds never run as root (exit 4). Profiles live in the catalog (0.3.0): a top-level profiles list and, per app, a map profile id to default / optional . --profile=NAME installs the profile's default members; --optional adds its optional ones. See catalog/README.md . Shells: an app may carry shells ( hyprland , plasma ). The running shell comes from XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP , overridable with --shell=hyprland|plasma|all . Non-matching apps are skipped: wrong_shell ; a named app still installs. Per-source steps source step pacman one pacman -S --needed call for all pacman apps (sudo shown in the plan) aur AUR helper (yay) as the normal user, apps one at a time pkgbuild PKGBUILD shown, makepkg as the normal user, result installed with pacman web a .desktop launcher in ~/.local/share/applications/bxcachy-<id>.desktop running brave --app=URL (written atomically, no package). The resolver adds brave to the plan when a web app is selected and brave is not installed. Result shape ( --json , inside the section 4 envelope) data for plan , install-plan and install : { "selection": { "mode": "default|ids|profile|optional", "ids": [], "profile": null }, "would_install": [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman", "targets": ["git"] } ], "done": [ { "id": "git", "source": "pacman" } ], "failed": [ { "id": "docker", "source": "pacman", "error": "target not found" } ], "skipped": [ { "id": "jq", "reason": "optional" } ] } plan and --dry-run fill would_install and leave done / failed empty. A real run fills done / failed and leaves would_install empty. Exit: 0 all done or nothing to do; 5 pacman phase failed, 6 AUR/pkgbuild phase failed (only when nothing succeeded); 7 some done and some failed. package-status ID exits 0 when installed, 1 when missing; data is { "id", "source", "installed": true|false } . package-source ID prints { "id", "source", "targets", "tier", "group" } . Human output is the same lists, one app per line with its source. Open questions Decided: a web app counts as installed when its launcher file exists. 12. Implemented so far, B2 (2026-11-09) Catalog 0.3.0: profiles , per-profile tier, shells (section 11, catalog/README.md ). Resolver class (selection) and Packages class (read-only commands). plan , install-plan , optional-plan , profile-plan , profile-install-plan , package-status , package-source , profile-list , desktop-list , tui-list , web-list , optional-list run on the catalog. Installed state comes from one pacman -Qq call (web apps: launcher file). install , optional-install , profile-install run on the catalog through Installer (one pacman -S call, yay per AUR app, pinned PKGBUILDs via git clone + makepkg -si ). Rules as in sections 2 and 11: no --yes prints the plan (exit 2), --dry-run exits 0, root with AUR or PKGBUILD builds exits 4 before any change, a named app without a source exits 3, partial results exit 7 (5 or 6 when nothing succeeded). Web apps install as launchers (see section 11 table). The 28 pkgbuild apps are pinned to one commit of omacom/omarchy-pkgs and install with git clone , git checkout COMMIT , makepkg -si as the normal user (root exits 4). All of them are optional, so a plain bxcachy install skips them. Not on the catalog: apps-doctor , dev-plan . 13. Desktop setup (decided with the owner 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10; all built) Builds on sections 2 to 4 (mutation rules, exit codes, --json ), the config service (section 6) and the Installer (argument arrays, done / failed / skipped ). Hyprland with Noctalia is installed beside KDE Plasma; KDE is never removed or reconfigured except what --keys hands over, which is backed up first. 13.1 Commands bxcachy setup hyprland [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] packages, images, starter configs, shortcut files bxcachy setup plasma [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] HyprKwin tiling on KDE Plasma bxcachy setup plasma --keys | --undo-keys hand Plasma's clashing keys over / back bxcachy setup hyprland --terminal=ghostty|kitty|alacritty|foot|konsole Super+Enter terminal (ghostty default) bxcachy setup hyprland --layout=dwindle|master|scrolling|floating default window layout in the starter hyprland.lua (dwindle default) bxcachy setup hyprland --workspaces=N --natural-scroll --layouts=us-intl,es --theme=dark|light|auto --wallpaper=box|grid|aurora|minimal starter choices (defaults: 2, off, us, dark, box); two or more keyboard layouts switch with Alt+Shift bxcachy setup terminal [--default=ghostty] [--also=kitty,foot,...] install terminals, starter configs with the Nerd Font bxcachy setup shell [--shell=zsh|fish|bash] Starship + shell init, login shell (zsh default) bxcachy setup xremap [--build=hypr|kde] [--yes] Cmd-style keys: AUR package, input access, user service bxcachy setup undo hyprland|plasma|xremap [--yes] remove only what setup added bxcachy setup status [--json] bxcachy tiling on|off|status HyprKwin inside Plasma, no logout bxcachy keys show | render xremap|hyprland|plasma | check | apply [--yes] [--dry-run] [--force] bxcachy assets list | install [--yes] [--dry-run] bxcachy session show | set hyprland|plasma [--yes] [--dry-run] bxcachy runner list | show | doctor | launch | select JSON | set P | menu-set P | launcher-command P JSON | menu-command P JSON the launcher abstraction (13.9) Every target runs, re-runs and undoes on its own; a re-run changes nothing when everything is in place. No --yes prints the plan (exit 2); --dry-run exits 0. Results as install : done / failed / skipped , exits 0, 2, 4 (precondition: root, wrong OS or CPU, no sudo, no Plasma, unsupported Plasma, X11, nothing to undo, session not installed), 5 (the pacman step failed), 6 (another step failed with nothing done), 7 (a step failed after earlier ones were done; later steps are skipped), 8 (config drift or lock). Never run as root: sudo is used only for the steps shown in the plan. --json is always one envelope on stdout (the config service has a quiet mode for that). Exception to --yes : tiling on|off acts at once (a reversible user setting meant to sit behind a shortcut). status exits 0 on, 1 off, 4 not installed. 13.2 setup plasma (HyprKwin) HyprKwin ( DGBooth/HyprKwin ) is a KWin script with Hyprland-style layouts and keys. It needs Plasma 6.6 or 6.8 on Wayland (6.7 warns, older or X11 exit 4). It is fetched pinned to a full commit (v1.2.0, 31abb63 , same rule as PKGBUILDs) into a temp directory and installed with its own tools/install.sh as the normal user, which backs up every global shortcut first. Plasma's keys stay Plasma's unless --keys (runs tools/hyprkwin-shortcuts.py apply ; --undo-keys restores). The animations effect needs one logout. setup undo plasma runs HyprKwin's uninstall. tiling on|off sets hyprkwinEnabled in kwinrc [Plugins] and asks KWin to reconfigure over D-Bus ( off also unloads the script). 13.3 setup hyprland Preconditions (exit 4): not root, pacman, CachyOS or Arch, x86_64, sudo. Steps, in order: packages : the missing ones of 18 official packages in one sudo pacman -S --needed call: hyprland , native noctalia , uwsm , hyprlock , hypridle , xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland , hyprpolkitagent , qt6ct , nwg-look , hyprpicker , grim , slurp , wl-clipboard , brightnessctl , kitty , adw-gtk-theme , noto-fonts , noto-fonts-emoji . Individual packages, never the CachyOS meta-package cachyos-hypr-noctalia (it conflicts with cachyos-desktop-settings , which the KDE session may rely on). Noctalia is the native noctalia package; noctalia-shell + noctalia-qs are a different Quickshell-based variant that conflicts with quickshell (a warning, not an error, if installed). The packages added are remembered ( $XDG_STATE/bxcachy/setup-hyprland.json , mode 600) so setup undo hyprland runs sudo pacman -Rs on exactly those. images : the logo and wallpapers (13.6), missing ones only. starter : the Noctalia config and palette, and a first hyprland.lua (13.5). keys : the shared shortcut files (13.4). 13.4 Shortcuts, keys and setup xremap One embedded table ( Shortcuts.bx ) holds the shortcuts and is rendered per target. The same keys work on Hyprland and Plasma [owner]: Part Hyprland Plasma Tiling and workspace keys Hyprland's own keys HyprKwin (same defaults) Cmd-style keys: Super+C, Super+V, Super+Tab xremap xremap Logout to the login screen, Super+Shift+Q hl.bind(... "uwsm stop") kglobalshortcutsrc [ksmserver] Log Out via kwriteconfig6 xremap, one shared YAML: Super+C/V send Ctrl+C/V, and Ctrl+Shift+C/V in terminals (a class list in the table); Super+Tab is a plain Alt+Tab remap [owner], answered on Hyprland by Noctalia's window switcher ( noctalia msg window-switcher hold ). keys render prints a target's text (pure). keys apply writes ~/.config/xremap/config.yml , ~/.config/hypr/bxcachy.lua and ~/.config/systemd/user/xremap.service through the config service (backup, journal; config list|diff|apply|restore cover them) and sets Plasma's Log Out with kwriteconfig6 when present. keys check reports clean / missing / outdated / drifted per piece (exit 0 or 1); a changed file is never overwritten without --force . Hyprland 0.55+ (Arch has 0.57) reads hyprland.lua ; hyprlang .conf is deprecated, so bxcachy targets Lua only [owner]. bxcachy.lua holds the Noctalia autostart and panel binds, the Alt+Tab switcher, the logout bind and the window and layer rules, taken from Noctalia's v5 Hyprland docs. bxcachy never edits the user's hyprland.lua : keys check reports not-loaded and keys apply prints the require("bxcachy") line to add (the starter file already has it). setup xremap installs xremap-hypr-bin or xremap-kde-bin with yay (build from --build , else the running desktop), adds the udev rule for /dev/uinput and the user to the input group (both remembered in setup-xremap.json , mode 600), writes the shortcut files and enables the user service; setup undo xremap reverses only what it added. It needs one logout. 13.5 Look and starter configs Ortus Brand Book 2025 palette (main #00FF78 , second #00DBFF , accent #FFF500 , dark #303446 , which is also Catppuccin Frappé's base) on Frappé neutrals [owner]. Starter.bx writes, through the config service and only what is missing (a Noctalia file the user changed is kept; hyprland.lua is written only when none exists): ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml and palettes/BxCachy.json ( NoctaliaConfig.bx ): dark theme with the custom palette; a top bar with launcher, workspaces and active window on the left; the clock, four world clocks (LAX, NYC, LON, MAD, editable clock widgets with a timezone ) and the media player in the centre; tray, network, bluetooth, volume, battery, notifications and control center on the right; the wallpaper folder. ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua from templates/hyprland.lua (embedded by bootstrap/gen-templates.sh ), based on Hyprland's own example: brand-gradient borders, rounded corners, blur, Hyprland's default animations, two persistent workspaces, natural scrolling off [owner, "inverse"], Super+Q closes a window (Cmd+Q habit), Super+Return terminal, Super+B browser, Super+E files, Super+F fullscreen, Super+Shift+3/4 screenshots, Super+Ctrl+Q lock, media keys, and require("bxcachy") . 13.5b Shell and terminal (decided 2026-11-10) Starship is the one prompt for every shell. setup shell installs the shell's packages in one sudo pacman call, writes ~/.config/starship.toml once (the official Catppuccin Powerline preset, Mocha palette, Nerd Font symbols; no question is asked, change it later with starship preset NAME -o ~/.config/starship.toml ; yours afterwards), and makes the chosen shell the login shell with sudo chsh . No Oh My Zsh and no plugin manager: plugins are pacman packages. zsh is the default ( zsh , zsh-autosuggestions , zsh-syntax-highlighting , zsh-completions ), then fish and bash . All get starship , fzf and zoxide , wired into the shell. zsh and bash load a managed ~/.config/bxcachy/shell.<shell> from one marked block appended to ~/.zshrc / ~/.bashrc (the rest of the file is never touched; the block is added once); fish gets ~/.config/fish/conf.d/bxcachy.fish (fish loads conf.d itself). The managed init is rewritten while unchanged and kept once you edit it. Terminals: ghostty (default), kitty , alacritty , foot , konsole . The default is the Super+Enter terminal in the starter hyprland.lua and the one setup hyprland installs (no longer Kitty); extras install with setup terminal --also= . Each terminal with a config file gets a starter written once that sets the Nerd Font ( JetBrainsMono Nerd Font ), so Starship's symbols render in any of them. The xremap terminal list already covers all five. Wizard keys: shell (default zsh ), terminal (default ghostty ), terminals_extra (default none). 13.6 Brand assets assets/ holds the sources ( build.py , composed from the official BoxLang icon in assets/brand/ , copied unchanged from Ortus-Solutions/ortus-artwork) and the rendered icon, logo and four wallpapers (box, grid, aurora, minimal). bootstrap/gen-assets.sh embeds them in AssetData.bx ; assets install writes them to ~/Pictures/BxCachy and ~/.local/share/bxcachy , never overwriting a file the user changed. They are written as base64 text and decoded with base64 -d because MatchBox's fileWrite turns a binary value into a string (upstream gap). 13.7 session session show lists the installed sessions, the one the login screen preselects, and any automatic login. session set hyprland|plasma makes that session the one SDDM preselects by rewriting Session= under [Last] in /var/lib/sddm/state.conf with sudo (a backup state.conf.bxcachy.bak is kept; the other lines stay). Hyprland prefers hyprland-uwsm.desktop . It never turns on automatic login (a warning if one is set, since it wins). There is no ask value: SDDM always remembers the last session. Log out with Super+Shift+Q to see the change. 13.9 runner : the launcher abstraction (port of the legacy bxcachy-runner ) Design (owner, 2026-11-10): BxCachy is built on an abstraction so runners can be switched. The rest of BxCachy asks for two things and never names a launcher: Runner.launch() open or toggle the launcher Runner.select( prompt, entries ) show [ { label, icon } ] in a menu, return the chosen position (0 = cancelled) Super+Space (Hyprland) is bound once, in the managed bxcachy.lua , to bxcachy runner launch (falling back to noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher when the chosen launcher cannot run), so runner set changes what Super+Space opens without ever editing a keybinding. Which launcher answers is a setting, recorded in ~/.config/bxcachy/runner.json (written atomically); the launcher and the menu provider are chosen separately. The runner never changes a keybinding or a desktop file ( doctor ends with Shortcut ownership: unchanged ). set and menu-set are user settings that act at once (no --yes ), like tiling . Providers are data in RunnerProviders (one descriptor each: id , title , package , launch argv, and menu : dmenu argv with {prompt} , icons , returns ). Adding a launcher is adding one descriptor. Provider Launch Menu (dmenu mode) Icons Choice comes back as Package noctalia (default on Hyprland) noctalia msg panel-toggle launcher none with Noctalia walker walker walker --dmenu no label Walker rofi (default menu) rofi -show drun rofi -dmenu -i -show-icons -format i -p yes index rofi fuzzel fuzzel fuzzel --dmenu --index --prompt yes index fuzzel wofi wofi --show drun wofi --dmenu --insensitive --prompt no label wofi vicinae vicinae toggle vicinae dmenu --prompt no label vicinae-bin (AUR) krunner krunner none with KDE system none (the desktop owns it) none custom your custom_command none select writes the labels (one per line, newlines inside a label become spaces) to a temporary file and runs the provider's command with it on stdin through sh -c 'exec "$@" < "$f"' . Providers that understand Rofi's extended dmenu protocol ( label NUL icon US name ) get icons; the others get plain labels. A non-zero exit, an empty answer, an unknown label or an index out of range is a cancel, never a wrong choice. bxcachy runner list | show | doctor | launch [--json] bxcachy runner set P | menu-set P bxcachy runner launcher-command P JSON_ARGV | menu-command P JSON_ARGV JSON argument arrays, {prompt} allowed bxcachy runner select JSON_ENTRIES [--prompt=TEXT] [--json] prints the 0-based index; exit 1 cancelled, 4 menu cannot run Commands are JSON argument arrays, never shell strings (a string, an empty array or an empty part exits 4). list marks the current choice with * ( --json adds each provider's title, package, icon support and answer format). doctor shows the commands and whether each executable is on PATH. launch starts the launcher detached (exit 4 for system or a missing program). The wizard offers Noctalia, Walker, Rofi, Fuzzel and Wofi; Vicinae, KRunner and custom work from the command line. hyprrunner was dropped (no package found, 2026-11-10). Fuzzel and Wofi flags are from their man pages. 13.10 db : local databases and search engines as containers (port of the legacy bxcachy-db and bxcachy-vector ) bxcachy db engines | list [--json] bxcachy db start ENGINE [--name N] [--port P] [--password-file FILE | --ask-password] [--yes] [--dry-run] create, or start a stopped one; never replaces a container bxcachy db stop|status|logs ENGINE [--name N] bxcachy db remove ENGINE [--name N] [--keep-data] --yes removes the container AND its data (volume and password file); --keep-data keeps the data bxcachy db info ENGINE [--name N] [--show-password] where it listens and how to connect (password masked by default) bxcachy db engine [podman|docker] which engine runs them (podman by default, saved in ~/.config/bxcachy/db.json) bxcachy db menu the control center, on the runner's menu provider (needs a terminal program) Exit codes: 0 done, 2 usage or no --yes (the plan is printed; --dry-run exits 0), 4 precondition (no container engine, unknown or unsupported engine, bad name or port, vm.max_map_count too low), 6 the container command failed. --json gives the standard envelope. Rules. Services listen on 127.0.0.1 only. A container that exists is never replaced (a stopped one is started; a running one is left alone). Containers are named bxcachy-db-<engine>-<name> (name defaults to default ; letters, digits and hyphens) and labelled io.bxcachy.database=true . Data lives in a named volume with the container's name, not a host folder ( db remove deletes it together with the container and the password files, so the next start is a clean database; --keep-data keeps them, and starting the same name again then reuses the volume and its password): rootless containers cannot write to a bind-mounted folder as the image's own user (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch and Meilisearch run as non-root). Choosing the password: by default one is generated. --password-file FILE uses the first line of a file you made; --ask-password asks twice at the terminal without echo ( /dev/tty , so it needs a terminal; the plan never prompts). A password is never a command-line value, so it cannot land in shell history or the process list. It must be 8 to 128 characters with no whitespace (OpenSearch also needs upper and lower case, a digit and a special character). It applies only when the container is created (the image sets it on first start of the data volume): a second start never changes it, an existing container refuses one, and a kept data volume (from remove --keep-data ) keeps the password it was made with (a different choice is refused). Engines without a password (Redis, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate) and Couchbase (set in its web console) refuse the options. The user name is fixed per engine ( postgres , root , admin , elastic ). Generated passwords (24 random bytes as hex) go in ~/.local/share/bxcachy/databases/<container>/ ( password and database.env , mode 600, plus meta.json with the port) and reach the container through --env-file , never on a command line. Nothing changes system settings: when vm.max_map_count is too low start stops with the sudo sysctl -w line to run. Images are pinned and were checked on Docker Hub on 2026-11-10 (Elasticsearch's from Elastic's docs). The method is detected ( --method overrides): chezmoi ( .chezmoiroot , .chezmoiignore , or dot_ / .chezmoi* names), then yadm ( .config/yadm/ , or ## alternate names), then stow ( .stowrc , .stow-local-ignore , or only top-level package folders that hold dotfiles), else links . Your dotfiles win, but nothing is replaced unasked. The plan splits the repo's files into new, already in place (a link to the repo, or an identical file) and conflicts (files you already have that would be replaced; chezmoi templates always count). apply --yes needs your approval of the conflicts: --overwrite , or a y at the prompt (read from /dev/tty , so a headless run without --overwrite exits 2 and changes nothing). Every replaced file is first moved into ~/.local/state/bxcachy/backups/dotfiles/<time>/ ; if a step then fails (exit 6) the originals are put back. status shows what was applied; undo --yes removes the links BxCachy made ( stow -D for stow) and restores the originals (for chezmoi and yadm only the originals come back: the files those tools created stay, remove them with the tool). Method Files go to your home by Applied with links one symlink per file (folders are never replaced by a link) ln -s stow each top-level folder is a package stow -d CLONE -t HOME -R PACKAGES chezmoi dot_ , private_ , executable_ , ... prefixes and .tmpl are mapped to the plain path for the conflict list chezmoi apply --source CLONE --force yadm ## alternate suffixes are mapped to the plain name yadm clone -f --no-bootstrap REPO ( yadm pull when it is already set up) Repo-only files ( .git , README* , LICENSE* , .gitignore , .stow-local-ignore ...) are never linked. A missing tool ( chezmoi , yadm , stow ; Arch extra ) is installed with sudo pacman -S --needed as the first step of apply (the plan says so). One repository can be set up at a time: a second one is refused (exit 4) until undo . Exits: 0 done, 2 no --yes or conflicts not approved, 4 precondition (cannot clone, unknown method, nothing to apply, tool not installable), 6 a step failed. The wizard's Import page asks for the repository (empty skips); init runs dotfiles apply REPO last , so your files win over the starter configs, and the conflict question appears at the terminal. Tested against real git repositories and fake tools ( stow , chezmoi , yadm , pacman ); the real tools have not been run. Private repositories and credentials are git's business (SSH keys or a credential helper must already work). 13.12 Apps: Basic or Customize, and your defaults (decided with the owner 2026-11-11) The wizard's Apps page asks how you want your apps : Basic (the default: an opinionated, recommended set) or Customize . Every machine uses the same commands; export / import (later) moves them between machines. Command Does secrets status backend in use, whether a keyring is available, how many secrets are stored secrets set NAME [--from-file=F] stores a value: typed hidden at the terminal, or read from a file. Never a command-line value. Replaces an existing one secrets list names only, with the coding agent that reads each known key secrets get NAME [--show] says whether it is set and its length; --show prints the value secrets unset NAME --yes deletes a value (plan without --yes , exit 2) secrets run [NAMES...] [--strict] -- CMD... runs CMD with those secrets in its own environment only; exit code is CMD's. A name that is not set is skipped, --strict exits 4 secrets env [NAMES...] prints export NAME='value' lines for eval (all stored names when none given) Names are environment variable names: capital letters, digits, underscores ( ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , OPENAI_API_KEY , GEMINI_API_KEY ). Backend: the desktop keyring through secret-tool (libsecret) when secret-tool exists and org.freedesktop.secrets is on the user D-Bus (running or activatable); otherwise private files ( ~/.local/share/bxcachy/secrets/NAME , mode 600 in a mode 700 folder). The choice is saved in ~/.config/bxcachy/secrets.json and shown by status . Keyring entries carry the attributes service=bxcachy name=NAME . Values are passed to secret-tool and to programs through standard input and the process environment, never through a command line, a temp file, a log, or answers.json . set is interactive on purpose and needs no --yes . Exit codes: 0 done, 2 usage or plan without --yes , 4 precondition (bad name, secret not set, no value), 6 the store failed. Loading into shells (default is per command, global is opt-in per key): secrets apply [--yes] writes ~/.config/bxcachy/secrets.sh (bash, zsh) and secrets.fish . They hold no values: one wrapper per agent command whose key is stored ( claude() { bxcachy secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- command claude "$@"; } ). secrets set runs it automatically. The shell init templates source these files. secrets global on NAME --yes | off NAME | show : exports a key to every new shell. on prints a warning first (every program, including AI agents and what they run, can read it). The values go to a session cache, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bxcachy-secrets.env and .fish (mode 600, tmpfs, wiped at logout), never to a config file. The loader files call secrets unlock once per login when the cache is missing (the keyring's single unlock prompt); secrets lock removes the cache. A globally exported key gets no wrapper. Moving machines and the keyring: secrets export FILE [--plain] [--force] --yes : all stored secrets as export NAME='value' lines, encrypted with a passphrase by age -p (age asks on the terminal; the file is mode 600). --plain writes a readable .env instead (mode 600; the plan says so). An existing file is kept unless --force . secrets import FILE [--overwrite] --yes : reads an age file or a .env file; the plan lists each name as new, same or differs. A name that already has a different value is kept unless --overwrite . New machine: install.sh , init --answers answers.json , secrets import , dotfiles apply . secrets setup [--keyring=kwallet|gnome-keyring|none] [--yes] [--dry-run] : checks for a Secret Service on the user D-Bus (running or activatable). Installs libsecret ( secret-tool , repo core) and age (repo extra) when missing; when no keyring exists, also kwallet on Plasma or gnome-keyring elsewhere, or the one named. --keyring=none installs no keyring and saves the file backend. The plan names what it installs. Package names and secret-tool in libsecret were checked on archlinux.org on 2026-11-11. Secret types and providers (decided with the owner 2026-11-11): Every secret has a type : ai (a key for an AI provider) or other (a GitHub token and so on). A name in the provider registry is ai automatically; any other name is other unless secrets set NAME --type=ai [--provider=ID] says otherwise. The type and provider are kept in secrets.json ( meta , names only, never values). secrets list [--type=ai|other] filters; secrets run --type=ai -- CMD loads every AI key and no other secret. The provider registry ( AiProviders ) maps providers to environment variables: anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , openai OPENAI_API_KEY , google GEMINI_API_KEY , openrouter OPENROUTER_API_KEY , novita NOVITA_API_KEY , opencode OPENCODE_API_KEY , groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, together ( GROQ_API_KEY , MISTRAL_API_KEY , DEEPSEEK_API_KEY , XAI_API_KEY , TOGETHER_API_KEY ). Names are from models.dev (the registry OpenCode uses), checked 2026-11-11. Each agent declares the providers it accepts ( AiAgents ): Claude Code anthropic, Codex openai, Gemini CLI google, OpenCode all of the above. An agent is only ever given keys from its own list. Its wrapper carries the stored ones among them ( opencode() { bxcachy secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY -- command opencode "$@"; } ); nothing else is loaded. Tests: tests/secrets-test.sh (fake secret-tool and busctl ). The registry of agent key names is from the vendors' documentation and the user can store any other valid name. 13.14 AI agents (decided with the owner 2026-11-11) bxcachy ai knows four coding agents ( AiAgents ): claude-code (command claude ), codex-cli ( codex ), gemini-cli ( gemini ), opencode-cli ( opencode ), each with the providers whose keys it accepts (see 13.13). It shows the BxCachy wordmark in the cyan to green gradient, the tagline and "Powered by BoxLang", checks the machine (CachyOS or Arch, not root, x86_64, sudo), downloads the channel's bxcachy-linux-x86_64 and bootstrap.tar.gz , verifies the Ed25519 signature of the release information ( version-latest.properties.sig , OpenSSL, public key embedded in the published script) and the SHA-256 of both files against it, runs the stages of bootstrap/install.sh ( packages , toolchains , binary --binary , core ) behind spinners, then the setup wizard. There is no custom menu: it installs everything the wizard's defaults call for. Log: ~/.cache/bxcachy/install.log . No human input: ... | bash -s -- --yes [--answers FILE] [--channel stable|beta] [--no-wizard] . --yes never asks (it needs passwordless sudo or a primed sudo -v ), the wizard then runs bxcachy init --answers FILE --yes or, without a file, bxcachy init --defaults --yes (the wizard's default answers). --dry-run shows the banner and checks and does nothing. --base-url or BXCACHY_BASE_URL points elsewhere. Exit 1 on any failure (nothing is installed after a failed checksum), 2 when you decline. Channels and S3 ( downloads.ortussolutions.com/ortussolutions/bxcachy/ ): stable/ (a v* tag), beta/ (every push to development , the bleeding edge), each with bxcachy-linux-x86_64 , .sha256 , bootstrap.tar.gz , .sha256 and version-latest.properties ( version , commit , sha256 , channel , builtAt ); snapshots/<version>-<sha>/ keeps every beta build and releases/<version>/ every stable one (uploads never delete). CI job 6 publishes when the AWS secrets exist ( AWS_ACCESS_KEY , AWS_ACCESS_SECRET ). update check [--notify] : compares the running binary's SHA-256 with the channel's version-latest.properties ; exit 10 when an update is available, 0 when current, 5 when the server is unreachable; also counts pending system updates ( checkupdates ). update apply [--yes] downloads the channel's binary, verifies its SHA-256 against its .sha256 and the signed release information, and replaces the installed binary atomically (exit 5 on a mismatch or a bad signature, the old binary stays). update channel [stable|beta] shows or sets the channel ( ~/.config/bxcachy/update.json ; the wizard asks update_channel , default stable). update notifications on|off|status manages a daily user timer bxcachy-update-check.timer that runs update check --notify and shows a notification ( noctalia msg notification-show , else notify-send ); the wizard asks update_notifications , default on. system update [--yes] takes a snapshot first when snapper or timeshift is present, then sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm and, with yay, yay -Sua --noconfirm . The menu has Settings entries for check, apply, both channels, notifications on and off, and system update. Signing (owner decision 2026-11-13: sign the installer and update): CI signs every version-latest.properties and install.sh with Ed25519 ( openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin ) using the secret BXCACHY_SIGNING_KEY ; the properties carry sha256 (binary) and bootstrap_sha256 (bundle). The public key is keys/release.pub (made with scripts/gen-signing-key.sh ), embedded into the binary ( bootstrap/gen-releasekey.sh writes src/bxcachy/ReleaseKey.bx ) and into the published install.sh (CI replaces @@PUBKEY_B64@@ ). With a key a missing or invalid signature, or a file that does not match the signed hash, stops the install or update before anything changes (exit 1 for the installer, 5 for update ); without a key (a development build) only SHA-256 is checked. Limit: the very first curl | bash still trusts the script it downloads (TLS and the bucket), so the signature protects the files the script fetches and every later update; verify install.sh.sig by hand with keys/release.pub for a stricter first install. Tests: tests/skills-test.sh (fake hub and agents), init_plan_test.bxs . 13.32 Themes, the Neovim layer and the Starship BoxLang module (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Command: theme list|show NAME|set NAME [--mode=theme|dark|light|auto] [--keep-wallpaper]|random|next|mode theme|dark|light|auto|install GIT_URL [--name=N] [--force]|import PATH [--name=N] [--force]|remove NAME|status , all with --dry-run where they change anything and --json . Like runner set these are settings: they act at once (no --yes ). Exit: 0 done, 2 bad usage or mode, 4 unknown or invalid theme (nothing is written), 6 a file could not be written. Theme format: an Omarchy theme folder, so themes move both ways: colors.toml , optional neovim.lua , optional backgrounds/ (the first file is the wallpaper). Both colors.toml shapes are read: the named one of Omarchy 4 master ( accent background foreground selection muted red green yellow blue magenta cyan bright_* , mode = "dark"|"light" ) and the older color0..color15 one. The named shape maps to the 16 ANSI slots as Omarchy's terminal templates do. A missing required key or a value that is not #rrggbb rejects the whole theme. Light or dark is the file's mode , else the background luminance (above 0.4 is light). Sources, first match wins: ~/.config/bxcachy/themes/NAME (installed or imported), ~/.config/omarchy/themes/NAME and ~/.local/share/omarchy/themes/NAME (found on disk), then 15 bundled in the binary: 10 from Omarchy (catppuccin, catppuccin-latte, tokyo-night, gruvbox, nord, rose-pine, kanagawa, everforest, matte-black, flexoki-light; MIT, credited in themes/NOTICE.md ) and 5 of ours ( bxcachy , bxcachy-light , bxcachy-midnight , bxcachy-cyan , bxcachy-forest ). install takes an https git URL only (a repository named omarchy-NAME-theme becomes NAME ), clones it shallow, validates it, refuses symlinks and an existing theme (without --force ), and copies it without .git . Only your own themes can be removed, never the current one. What set writes (through the config service: atomic, backed up, journalled; unchanged files are skipped): the Noctalia palette ~/.config/noctalia/palettes/BxCachyTheme.json (the 16 roles are derived from the theme, both variants carry the same colours), ~/.config/bxcachy/theme/{ghostty,kitty.conf,alacritty.toml,foot.ini,hypr.lua} , ~/.config/btop/themes/bxcachy.theme , ~/.local/state/bxcachy/current/theme/neovim.lua and every theme's neovim.lua in ~/.config/bxcachy/nvim-themes/ . Then it tells the desktop: noctalia msg color-scheme-set custom BxCachyTheme , theme-mode-set , wallpaper-set (a bundled BxCachy theme brings one of our wallpapers, an on-disk theme its backgrounds/ , other bundled themes keep yours), plasma-apply-colorscheme BreezeDark|BreezeLight on KDE, hyprctl reload inside Hyprland. A missing or silent Noctalia is a note, not an error. Mode theme (default) follows the theme; dark , light or auto pin it; the mode survives set . Where the files are used: the terminal starters (written once) include ~/.config/bxcachy/theme/... (ghostty config-file = ?path , kitty include , alacritty [general] import , foot include= ) and TerminalConfig.apply writes the default theme files, so an include never points at nothing; your own terminal configs are never edited. The managed hypr/bxcachy.lua reads theme/hypr.lua (border colours). btop needs color_theme = "bxcachy" in your btop.conf , which we do not edit. Not themed in v1: the Starship prompt (fixed Catppuccin Mocha palette, no include mechanism), VS Code, Chromium, GTK and Qt apps (whether noctalia msg templates-apply themes them is unverified). Neovim layer ( editor lazyvim|boxlang|status|refresh ): after the starter is cloned (an existing ~/.config/nvim is never touched) the layer is added: lua/config/bxcachy.lua (relativenumber off, autoformat off, OSC 52 clipboard over SSH, loaded by one line added to options.lua ), lua/plugins/bxcachy.lua (no news popups, no scroll animation, transparent lualine), plugin/after/bxcachy-transparency.lua , lua/plugins/boxlang.lua ( ortus-boxlang/vim-boxlang , loaded at startup so its ftdetect runs first), lua/plugins/bxcachy-themes.lua (every theme's colourscheme plugin listed lazily from nvim-themes/ ), lua/plugins/bxcachy-theme-reload.lua (a libuv watcher re-applies the colourscheme when the theme file changes), lua/plugins/theme.lua (a link to the current theme's neovim.lua ) and the neo-tree extra merged into lazyvim.json . It is modelled on Omarchy's omarchy-nvim package, written by us. editor boxlang adds only the plugin file to a LazyVim config you have. refresh rewrites the files still as BxCachy wrote them and keeps the ones you changed unless --force . Wizard: theme_name (default bxcachy ; a Light answer with the default picks bxcachy-light ) runs theme set after the terminals, optional, for Hyprland and Plasma; the editor answer now includes the layer and BoxLang syntax. The Themes menu has next, random, the five BxCachy themes, the four modes and status. Starship: the starter prompt shows the BoxLang version like Java: custom.boxlang ( ${custom.boxlang} in the format), shown only in a directory with .bx .bxs .bxm .cfc .cfm .cfs files or box.json , Application.bx , Application.cfc . It has no when (Starship shows a custom module when ANY of when , detect_files , detect_extensions matches, so when would show it everywhere); its command prints the ~/.bvm/current symlink name (honouring BVM_HOME ) or nothing. The starter is written once, so existing installs see the change with bxcachy config diff starship . Verified and not: tested with fake noctalia , plasma-apply-colorscheme , hyprctl , git , pacman ( tests/theme-test.sh , tests/editor-test.sh , tests/theme_colors_test.bxs , tests/init_plan_test.bxs ); the Lua files only parse-checked and the theme loader run against a stub vim (no Neovim here); the Starship command logic run in sh , not by Starship. Unverified on a real machine: the Noctalia IPC argument forms against a running Noctalia, Hyprland's dofile and hl.config from the managed module and hyprctl reload with a Lua config, ghostty's ? optional include, kitty, alacritty [general] import and foot include= with a missing file, the foot [colors-dark] section on the installed foot, lazy.nvim picking the colourscheme plugin up on :colorscheme , vim-boxlang loading with lazy = false , Starship hiding a custom module on empty output. 13.33 Virtual machines: Windows and Linux desktops in containers (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Command: vm list|status [NAME]|size [NAME]|info NAME [--show-password]|doctor|versions linux|windows|create windows [NAME] [--version=V] [--ram=] [--cpus=] [--disk=] [--share=PATH|none]|create linux NAME [--tag=T] [--cpus=] [--memory=] [--share=PATH|none] [--gpu=none|auto|intel|amd|nvidia]|start|stop|logs NAME|open NAME [--web] [--fullscreen]|remove NAME [--keep-data] , with --json . create and remove are plans until --yes ( --dry-run too). Exit: 0 done, 2 plan or bad usage, 4 precondition (bad name or version, KVM unusable, no engine, no terminal to choose a Windows version on, GPU not possible), 6 a command failed. Two kinds, any number of each. Every VM has a name ( [a-z0-9-] , up to 31) and a record in ~/.config/bxcachy/vms/NAME.json (mode 600). Windows is dockurr/windows ; a Linux desktop is LinuxServer's lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:TAG . The container is bxcachy-vm-NAME , labelled io.bxcachy.vm . The first Windows is named windows . The engine is the one bxcachy db engine chose (Podman by default). Where things live (documented for the user in docs/guides/vms.md ): data in ~/.local/share/bxcachy/vms/NAME ( storage is the Windows disk, config is the Linux desktop's home folder), the record above, the password in the keyring as BXCACHY_VM_<NAME>_PASSWORD ( bxcachy secrets ), an app-menu launcher ~/.local/share/applications/bxcachy-vm-NAME.desktop (runs vm open NAME ), and a shared folder: ~/Windows (drive Z:) or ~/Shared ( /config/Shared ), or --share=none . remove deletes the container, the data, the password, the record and the launcher; the shared folder is never deleted; --keep-data keeps data, password and record. size is du of the data folder; the images are in the engine ( podman image ls ). Security: ports bind to 127.0.0.1 only (the webtop terminal has passwordless sudo; the Windows web viewer and RDP are for you). The password is generated (16 random bytes), stored in the keyring, and reaches the container through an env file (mode 600) that is deleted right after run . The default admin password of dockur is never used. Ports: Linux 3001 upward (HTTPS, a self-signed certificate: accept it once); Windows web viewer 8006 upward and RDP 3389 upward (TCP and UDP); each VM takes the first port no record uses and nothing listens on. Windows: --version takes any dockur VERSION value (25, vm versions windows ). Without it at a terminal, a picker shows ten choices with sizes and notes (11 Pro, 11 LTSC, 11 Enterprise, 10 Pro, 10 LTSC, Tiny11, Tiny11 Core, Tiny10, Server 2025 and 2022; the Tiny builds are marked UNOFFICIAL); with no terminal it exits 4 (a script passes --version ; with --json the picker text goes to the terminal device, never stdout). Defaults: RAM half the machine (4G to 8G), CPUs half (2 to 8), disk 64G. Run: --device /dev/kvm --device /dev/net/tun --cap-add NET_ADMIN --stop-timeout 120 , env VERSION RAM_SIZE CPU_CORES DISK_SIZE USERNAME PASSWORD . The install downloads the ISO inside the container on the first start (3 to 8 GB) and takes a while; you need your own Windows license (dockur uses generic trial keys that do not activate). open starts the VM if needed, waits for RDP, then runs the first FreeRDP client found ( sdl-freerdp3 , sdl-freerdp , xfreerdp3 , xfreerdp , wlfreerdp3 , wlfreerdp ) with /args-from:file:PATH : a mode 600 file holding /v: /u: /p: /cert:ignore +clipboard /dynamic-resolution /title: (and /f ), so the password is never on a command line; the file is removed after 15 seconds. While Windows is still installing, open says so and points at open --web (the browser viewer). Linux: 21 tags from the webtop page (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch: xfce, kde, mate, i3, and lxqt for Ubuntu; Alpine with the upstream latest tag as alpine-xfce ); default ubuntu-xfce . The dev tag and the deprecated Enterprise Linux tags are not offered; KDE tags are Wayland only. Run: --shm-size 1gb , env PUID PGID TZ CUSTOM_USER=bxcachy PASSWORD , -v data:/config . Rootless Podman maps the container's root to you, so PUID and PGID are 0 there (files stay yours); Docker uses your ids. --cpus and --memory map to the engine flags. When the host has no IPv6 ( /proc/sys/net/ipv6 missing) the container also gets DISABLE_IPV6=true , because the image's nginx otherwise fails on listen [::] (found by running the real image; doctor notes it). GPU (Linux desktops, opt-in): intel and amd add --device /dev/dri (needs it to exist); auto does that when /dev/dri exists and nothing otherwise; nvidia follows the webtop docs: Docker gets --runtime nvidia --gpus all --device /dev/nvidia-modeset , Podman gets CDI ( --device nvidia.com/gpu=all --device /dev/nvidia-modeset ). The Alpine tags refuse NVIDIA. doctor reports /dev/dri , the NVIDIA driver version (the docs ask for 580 or newer) and nvidia-ctk . Windows has no GPU option. Wizard and menu: two optional questions after the databases: vm_windows (none or one of the ten, with descriptions) and vm_linux (none or six tags); they become optional steps vm create windows --version=V and vm create linux desktop --tag=T , and add the Podman install when no engine answer was given. The menu has a Virtual machines entry (list, sizes, doctor, the two version tables). Verified and not: tested against fake Podman and Docker (every run argument, files, modes, ports, passwords, launchers, exit codes) in tests/vm-test.sh and tests/init_plan_test.bxs . Also run for real (2026-11-13, a sandbox with Docker 29.9.2, no KVM, no IPv6, running as root): vm create linux with the real lscr.io/linuxserver/webtop:ubuntu-xfce image through bxcachy : the published 127.0.0.1:3001 answers 401 without credentials, 200 with the generated password and 401 with a wrong one; the shared folder works both ways; start , stop , status , size , info , open (browser launch only) and remove behave. Never run: Windows (no /dev/kvm here), Podman, a non-root user (so PUID and file ownership are untested), GPUs, FreeRDP. Unverified on a real machine: Windows booting under rootless Podman ( /dev/kvm , /dev/net/tun , NET_ADMIN ), RDP through the published 127.0.0.1 port (dockur documents the container's own IP too), dockur on a Btrfs disk (CachyOS default; not checked in its README), webtop under rootless Podman with PUID 0 and as a non-root Docker user, the NVIDIA paths (driver 580 or newer from a .run file per the docs, whether CachyOS's packaged driver counts, CDI on Podman, the Arch package name nvidia-container-toolkit ), and the FreeRDP argument file ( /args-from:file: read from the FreeRDP 3 source, the client binary names are a best guess). 13.34 The menu, package search and remove (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) Menu skeleton. bxcachy menu follows Omarchy's 11 sections and adds one of ours: Apps, Install, Remove, Appearance, Trigger, Setup, Update, Develop (BoxLang, databases, virtual machines, containers, the editor), Agent, Learn, About, System. What used to be top-level BxCachy entries are folded in: Themes into Appearance, Notifications and Screenshot into Trigger, Cloud storage and Settings into Setup, Web apps into Install and Remove. The tree is MenuTree (data); menu items [--json] prints it, menu search TEXT [--json] lists the entries whose path matches with the command each runs (the CLI mirror of the in-menu search). Omarchy's menu has 362 actions; ours had 63 and now has 136 (the Appearance, Trigger, Setup, Update and System depth is still to come, see the parity plan). Search. The first entry of the top level is Search… : one flat list of every entry as a path ("Appearance > Next theme"); the menu provider filters as you type, and the choice runs exactly as it would from its section. Entry kinds: sub , spawn (detached), run (in a terminal, waits for Enter: output and sudo prompts), open (xdg-open a URL), pick (choose from a live list, then run with {} replaced), ask (type a line, then run), pkgsearch (type, choose a package from the repos or the AUR, confirm, pkg install in a terminal), catalog (one catalog group, choose, confirm, install ID --yes in a terminal), db , webcreate , webrm . A confirm asks before running (reboot, shutdown, logout, every removal). Live lists: themes (the current one marked ✓), your themes, installed browsers, terminals and file managers, explicit packages, installed catalog apps, VMs, installed skills. Providers that cannot take typed text open a terminal that asks ( bxcachy web add ) or say what to type. pkg : pkg search TEXT [--source=all|repo|aur] [--limit=40] (pacman -Ss and the AUR RPC v5 search/TEXT?by=name-desc ; exact names first, then repo packages, then AUR by popularity; installed ones marked; an AUR outage is a note, repo results stay), pkg info NAME , pkg installed [--explicit] , pkg install NAME... [--aur] [--yes] (repo packages through the existing installer steps, AUR packages through yay -S --needed --noconfirm ; never as root for the AUR, exit 4 without yay; the plan warns that AUR packages are user-submitted scripts and points at yay -G NAME ), pkg remove NAME... [--yes] ( pacman -Rns --noconfirm , one package at a time). Protected and never removed: base, pacman, sudo, systemd, glibc, bash, coreutils, filesystem, linux-firmware, grub, util-linux, shadow, the keyrings, linux* kernels and their headers and NVIDIA modules, and the cachyos-settings , cachyos-hooks and mirrorlist packages. Not-installed names are a no-op. Names are validated ( [a-z0-9@._+-] ), search text too. remove ID_OR_PACKAGE... : a catalog id removes what installing it put there (pacman, AUR and PKGBUILD apps: their targets through pkg remove ; web apps: the launcher file); a vendor-script app is reported with exit 4 ("use its own uninstaller"); anything that is not a catalog id is taken as a package name. A plan until --yes ; your files in ~/.config and ~/.local are never touched. system lock|suspend|logout|reboot|shutdown : through noctalia msg session ... inside Hyprland with Noctalia (Noctalia IPC docs), else loginctl lock-session , systemctl suspend|reboot|poweroff , loginctl terminate-session . Lock and suspend act at once; logout, reboot and shutdown are a plan until --yes (the menu asks first). Verified: tests/pkg-test.sh (fake pacman, yay, curl, sudo, id) and tests/menu-test.sh (fake Rofi, Wofi and terminal); pkg search|info|install|remove and remove were also run against the real Arch repos and the live AUR in the Arch test container (search, install and remove of cowsay , jq removed by catalog id, protected packages refused). Not verified: the menu on a real provider (Rofi, Walker, Fuzzel), AUR installs through yay , system actions on a real session. 13.35 Appearance (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxcachy appearance status|apply and verbs bar show|hide|toggle|position top|bottom|left|right|style opaque|glassy|clear|clock ID|battery on|off , dock show|hide|toggle|mode always|autohide|off|position bottom|left|right , windows gaps on|off|corners theme|rounded|sharp|opacity opaque|glassy|one-window-ratio on|off , animations on|off , layout dwindle|scrolling|floating , font list|ID|install ID , background list|set NAME_OR_PATH|next|random . Everything that changes the system is a plan (exit 2) without --yes . auto on|off|status follows your location by itself. It installs geoclue (extra) and automatic-timezoned (AUR, 2.0.163). The AUR package ships no systemd unit and the daemon needs GeoClue to run without an agent (its README), so auto on writes /etc/systemd/system/automatic-timezoned.service (runs as root, which may set the zone without a polkit rule) and /etc/geoclue/conf.d/90-bxcachy-timezone.conf ( [agent] whitelist= empty; [automatic-timezoned] allowed, system, any user), then systemctl enable --now . auto off disables the service and removes both files. The plan states the privacy tradeoff: GeoClue looks up your location online (Wi-Fi networks or IP address). Not verified on a real machine: the geoclue drop-in being read from conf.d , the daemon getting a location without an agent, and tzupdate flags (we run it with none). If the zone does not change, journalctl -u automatic-timezoned . Menu: Setup > Time. Verified: tests/time-test.sh (fake timedatectl, systemctl, sudo, pacman, yay, tzupdate). 13.39 Toggles, DNS, kernels and security (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) bxcachy toggle stay-awake [on|off] runs noctalia msg caffeine-enable|disable|toggle (Noctalia IPC docs). Without Noctalia it exits 4 (on Plasma use System Settings > Power Management). Noctalia has no screensaver, so there is no screensaver toggle; notify dnd|snooze already cover reminders. bxcachy dns [cloudflare|google|quad9|dhcp|custom IP[,IP...]] lists or sets the DNS servers of the active NetworkManager connections (loopback, bridge, tunnel and container devices are skipped) with nmcli connection modify NAME ipv4.dns ... ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes ipv6.dns ... ipv6.ignore-auto-dns yes , then connection up NAME . dhcp clears them. A plan (exit 2) without --yes ; a bad IP exits 2. bxcachy kernel list|install NAME|remove NAME . list shows the running kernel, the installed kernel packages and the linux-cachyos* kernels you could add (nvidia, zfs, rc and headers packages are left out). install is sudo pacman -S --needed NAME NAME-headers (the name must match linux(-[a-z0-9]+)* and exist in the repos, else exit 4 or 2). remove refuses the running kernel (judged from uname -r and the package suffix) and the last installed kernel (exit 4). It never edits the bootloader and never picks the default: the boot entries come from the kernel packages' hooks and you choose in the boot menu. bxcachy security status|fingerprint|fido2|ssh-server|passwordless-sudo . Guards: only /etc/pam.d/sudo is ever changed (never login, SDDM or the lock screen); the line is auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so or auth sufficient pam_u2f.so cue inserted before the first auth line and marked with a # bxcachy KIND comment, so your password still works without the reader or key; a file with no auth line is left alone (exit 4); the original is kept once as /etc/pam.d/sudo.bxcachy-backup ; off removes exactly the marked line; running on twice adds one line. fingerprint enroll runs fprintd-enroll ; fido2 register runs pamu2fcfg into ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys , and fido2 on refuses (exit 4) until that file exists. passwordless-sudo on writes /etc/sudoers.d/50-bxcachy-nopasswd ( USER ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL , user from $USER` and checked against `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$ ) only after visudo -cf passes, with mode 440; off removes it. ssh-server on|off installs openssh and runs systemctl enable|disable --now sshd.service . Everything is a plan (exit 2) without --yes , and --dry-run prints the exact line or file. Agents: the Agent menu runs ai launch NAME ; there is no separate agent command. Menu: Trigger > Toggle (stay awake), Setup > DNS, Security, Time, Kernel. Verified: tests/tweaks-test.sh and tests/security-test.sh (fake nmcli, pacman, noctalia, uname, visudo, sudo and fake /etc/pam.d and /etc/sudoers.d ). Not verified on a real machine: PAM behavior with a real reader or key, nmcli on your connection names, kernel removal. 13.40 The command reference and bxcachy help (decided with the owner 2026-11-13) One source: docs/reference/cli.json holds, for every command, its group, a one-sentence summary, its usage lines, examples, whether it needs --yes ( mutates ) and an optional note. bootstrap/gen-docs.sh writes docs/reference/commands.md (the docs page: flags, exit codes, the JSON envelope, an index by group, then every command with usage and examples) and src/bxcachy/HelpData.bx (the same data inside the binary). bxcachy help (and bare bxcachy ) lists every command by group with its summary; bxcachy help NAME prints the summary, usage, whether --yes is needed, examples and notes; --json returns the same data; an unknown name exits 2. Drift checks: gen-docs.sh --check fails when a command in src/Main.bx has no entry, an entry has no command, a usage line does not start with its command, an example names no real command, a summary does not end in a full stop, or the text contains an em dash. NFS needs neither. Names are ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$ . shares NAME lists SMB shares with smbclient -g -L HOST -A AUTHFILE (the auth file is a private temp file, deleted after; no password on a command line; IPC$ and other hidden shares are dropped) or NFS exports with showmount -e --no-headers . mount|unmount NAME SHARE mounts at ~/NAS/NAME/LEAF ( BXCACHY_NAS_HOME overrides) with sudo mount -t cifs|nfs ; the SMB options are credentials=/etc/bxcachy/nas/NAME.cred,uid,gid,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0600,dir_mode=0700 plus vers= only when you set one (otherwise the kernel negotiates the highest version both sides support). Exit 4 when a check fails. sync NAME SRC --to=SHARE[/PATH] is a plain rsync -a mirror to a mounted share. Nothing is deleted from the NAS unless you add --delete , and the plan says so in capitals. use NAME SHARE [--path=bxcachy-backup] records targets.nas-NAME in ~/.config/bxcachy/backup.json ( {type: nas, nas, share, path} ); backup data setup reads it. Verified: tests/nas-test.sh with fake avahi-browse, smbclient, showmount, findmnt, rsync, sudo and a fake /etc . Not verified on a real Synology: DSM share permissions, SMB signing, NFS export options, nss-mdns name resolution. 14. Install and the setup wizard (decided with the owner 2026-11-10; install, wizard and the init engine are built, the pages' later commands are not) 14.1 Install bootstrap/install.sh [--yes] [--dry-run] is the one install command. Bun and Deno are catalog apps ( install bun deno ). 14.2 bxcachy init A full-screen terminal wizard that asks the questions below, shows a review screen, then runs the matching commands. Answers are saved to ~/.config/bxcachy/answers.json (mode 600, written atomically); a re-run starts from the saved answers. bxcachy init the wizard (needs a terminal) bxcachy init --answers FILE [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] headless: no TUI, the plan from FILE; same --yes / --dry-run rules as every mutating verb bxcachy init --print-answers the saved answers Exits: as setup (0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8); 4 also for no terminal without --answers .
