### 13.38 Time zone (decided with the owner 2026-11-13)

* **`bxcachy time status|zone|sync|auto|ntp`.** `zone` shows the zone, `zone --list` lists them, `zone ZONE` sets it (`sudo timedatectl set-timezone`, validated against `timedatectl list-timezones`; exit 4 for an unknown one). `sync` sets the zone once from your IP address with `tzupdate` (AUR, installed first when missing): the command to run after you land. `ntp on|off` is `timedatectl set-ntp`. Everything that changes the system is a plan (exit 2) without `--yes`.
* **`auto on|off|status`** follows your location by itself. It installs `geoclue` (extra) and `automatic-timezoned` (AUR, 2.0.163). The AUR package ships no systemd unit and the daemon needs GeoClue to run without an agent (its README), so `auto on` writes `/etc/systemd/system/automatic-timezoned.service` (runs as root, which may set the zone without a polkit rule) and `/etc/geoclue/conf.d/90-bxcachy-timezone.conf` (`[agent] whitelist=` empty; `[automatic-timezoned]` allowed, system, any user), then `systemctl enable --now`. `auto off` disables the service and removes both files. The plan states the privacy tradeoff: GeoClue looks up your location online (Wi-Fi networks or IP address).
* **Not verified on a real machine:** the geoclue drop-in being read from `conf.d`, the daemon getting a location without an agent, and `tzupdate` flags (we run it with none). If the zone does not change, `journalctl -u automatic-timezoned`.
* **Menu:** Setup \> Time. **Verified:** `tests/time-test.sh` (fake timedatectl, systemctl, sudo, pacman, yay, tzupdate).

### 13.39 Toggles, DNS, kernels and security (decided with the owner 2026-11-13)

* **`bxcachy toggle stay-awake [on|off]`** runs `noctalia msg caffeine-enable|disable|toggle` (Noctalia IPC docs). Without Noctalia it exits 4 (on Plasma use System Settings \> Power Management). Noctalia has no screensaver, so there is no screensaver toggle; `notify dnd|snooze` already cover reminders.
* **`bxcachy dns [cloudflare|google|quad9|dhcp|custom IP[,IP...]]`** lists or sets the DNS servers of the active NetworkManager connections (loopback, bridge, tunnel and container devices are skipped) with `nmcli connection modify NAME ipv4.dns ... ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes ipv6.dns ... ipv6.ignore-auto-dns yes`, then `connection up NAME`. `dhcp` clears them. A plan (exit 2) without `--yes`; a bad IP exits 2.
* **`bxcachy kernel list|install NAME|remove NAME`.** `list` shows the running kernel, the installed kernel packages and the `linux-cachyos*` kernels you could add (nvidia, zfs, rc and headers packages are left out). `install` is `sudo pacman -S --needed NAME NAME-headers` (the name must match `linux(-[a-z0-9]+)*` and exist in the repos, else exit 4 or 2). `remove` refuses the running kernel (judged from `uname -r` and the package suffix) and the last installed kernel (exit 4). It never edits the bootloader and never picks the default: the boot entries come from the kernel packages' hooks and you choose in the boot menu.
* **`bxcachy security status|fingerprint|fido2|ssh-server|passwordless-sudo`.** Guards: only `/etc/pam.d/sudo` is ever changed (never login, SDDM or the lock screen); the line is `auth sufficient pam_fprintd.so` or `auth sufficient pam_u2f.so cue` inserted before the first `auth` line and marked with a `# bxcachy KIND` comment, so your password still works without the reader or key; a file with no `auth` line is left alone (exit 4); the original is kept once as `/etc/pam.d/sudo.bxcachy-backup`; `off` removes exactly the marked line; running `on` twice adds one line. `fingerprint enroll` runs `fprintd-enroll`; `fido2 register` runs `pamu2fcfg` into `~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys`, and `fido2 on` refuses (exit 4) until that file exists. `passwordless-sudo on` writes `/etc/sudoers.d/50-bxcachy-nopasswd` (`USER ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL`, user from ``$USER` and checked against `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$``) only after `visudo -cf` passes, with mode 440; `off` removes it. `ssh-server on|off` installs openssh and runs `systemctl enable|disable --now sshd.service`. Everything is a plan (exit 2) without `--yes`, and `--dry-run` prints the exact line or file.
* **Agents:** the Agent menu runs `ai launch NAME`; there is no separate `agent` command.
* **Menu:** Trigger \> Toggle (stay awake), Setup \> DNS, Security, Time, Kernel. **Verified:** `tests/tweaks-test.sh` and `tests/security-test.sh` (fake nmcli, pacman, noctalia, uname, visudo, sudo and fake `/etc/pam.d` and `/etc/sudoers.d`). Not verified on a real machine: PAM behavior with a real reader or key, `nmcli` on your connection names, kernel removal.

### 13.40 The command reference and `bxcachy help` (decided with the owner 2026-11-13)

* **One source:** `docs/reference/cli.json` holds, for every command, its group, a one-sentence summary, its usage lines, examples, whether it needs `--yes` (`mutates`) and an optional note. `bootstrap/gen-docs.sh` writes `docs/reference/commands.md` (the docs page: flags, exit codes, the JSON envelope, an index by group, then every command with usage and examples) and `src/bxcachy/HelpData.bx` (the same data inside the binary).
* **`bxcachy help`** (and bare `bxcachy`) lists every command by group with its summary; `bxcachy help NAME` prints the summary, usage, whether `--yes` is needed, examples and notes; `--json` returns the same data; an unknown name exits 2.
* **Drift checks:** `gen-docs.sh --check` fails when a command in `src/Main.bx` has no entry, an entry has no command, a usage line does not start with its command, an example names no real command, a summary does not end in a full stop, or the text contains an em dash. The usage lines of older commands are copied from the usage text in `src/Main.bx`; the newer classes (`appearance`, `display`, `power`, `time`, `toggle`, `dns`, `kernel`, `security`) print their own usage, so their entries are written by hand and must be updated with the class.
* **Verified:** `tests/help-test.sh` (the groups, a command, JSON, unknown, and that the generated files are current).

### 13.41 NAS as a first-class namespace (decided with the owner 2026-11-13)

* **`bxcachy nas`** keeps every NAS you use in `~/.config/bxcachy/nas.json` (name, host, protocol `smb` or `nfs`, user, optional SMB version, and the shares you mounted). `discover` browses the network with `avahi-browse -rtp _smb._tcp` and `_nfs._tcp` (IPv4 only). `setup` installs `cifs-utils nfs-utils smbclient avahi nss-mdns rsync` and enables `avahi-daemon` (a plan without `--yes`; every tool was checked in the Arch repos and its binary exists after install).
* **`add NAME --host=H`** needs `--user` and a password for SMB (`--ask-password`, typed hidden, or `--password-file=F`); the password goes to the keyring as `BXCACHY_NAS_<NAME>_PASSWORD` and never into `nas.json`. NFS needs neither. Names are `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$`.
* **`shares NAME`** lists SMB shares with `smbclient -g -L HOST -A AUTHFILE` (the auth file is a private temp file, deleted after; no password on a command line; `IPC$` and other hidden shares are dropped) or NFS exports with `showmount -e --no-headers`.
* **`mount|unmount NAME SHARE`** mounts at `~/NAS/NAME/LEAF` (`BXCACHY_NAS_HOME` overrides) with `sudo mount -t cifs|nfs`; the SMB options are `credentials=/etc/bxcachy/nas/NAME.cred,uid,gid,iocharset=utf8,file_mode=0600,dir_mode=0700` plus `vers=` only when you set one (otherwise the kernel negotiates the highest version both sides support). **The credentials file is root-only (mode 600) because `mount.cifs` reads it as root**; the plan says so.
* **`auto on|off NAME SHARE`** writes `<escaped-path>.mount` and `.automount` units to `/etc/systemd/system` (`Options=...,nofail`, `TimeoutSec=20`, `TimeoutIdleSec=600`, wanted by `multi-user.target`), runs `daemon-reload` and `enable --now`, so a sleeping NAS never blocks login. `off` disables and removes them; a NAS with automatic mounts is not removed (exit 4) until they are off.
* **`test NAME [SHARE]`** checks: reachable (TCP 445 or 2049), signed in or exports readable, mounted (`findmnt`), writable (a probe file), free space. Exit 4 when a check fails.
* **`sync NAME SRC --to=SHARE[/PATH]`** is a plain `rsync -a` mirror to a mounted share. Nothing is deleted from the NAS unless you add `--delete`, and the plan says so in capitals.
* **`use NAME SHARE [--path=bxcachy-backup]`** records `targets.nas-NAME` in `~/.config/bxcachy/backup.json` (`{type: nas, nas, share, path}`); `backup data setup` reads it.
* **Verified:** `tests/nas-test.sh` with fake avahi-browse, smbclient, showmount, findmnt, rsync, sudo and a fake `/etc`. **Not verified on a real Synology:** DSM share permissions, SMB signing, NFS export options, `nss-mdns` name resolution.

## 14. Install and the setup wizard (decided with the owner 2026-11-10; install, wizard and the init engine are built, the pages' later commands are not)

### 14.1 Install

`bootstrap/install.sh [--yes] [--dry-run]` is the one install command. It prints the plan, asks one `Proceed? [Y/n]` at a terminal (without a terminal it needs `--yes`, else exit 2; `--dry-run` exits 0), then runs, in order: packages with yay and Rust, toolchains (mvm, bvm, BoxLang, nvm and Node, MatchBox), the bxcachy binary, and the core apps (`bxcachy profile-install core --yes`). External installer scripts run without a gate (section 2, rule 8). `install.sh check` is the read-only report; `packages|toolchains|binary|core --yes` re-run one stage. When the wizard exists the install ends by starting it at a terminal.

**Required vs optional toolchains (decided 2026-11-10):** the install always adds BoxLang (Java 21, bvm, mvm, MatchBox, Rust). nvm and Node.js are no longer part of it; they are the optional JavaScript toolchain: `bxcachy toolchain node [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]` runs the pinned nvm installer from `box.json` `toolchain.nvm` (an external script: its URL is in the plan, it adds nvm to your shell startup files) and `nvm install lts/*`, skipping what is already there. Bun and Deno are catalog apps (`install bun deno`).

### 14.2 `bxcachy init`

A full-screen terminal wizard that asks the questions below, shows a review screen, then runs the matching commands. Answers are saved to `~/.config/bxcachy/answers.json` (mode 600, written atomically); a re-run starts from the saved answers.

    bxcachy init                          the wizard (needs a terminal)
    bxcachy init --answers FILE [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]    headless: no TUI, the plan from FILE; same --yes / --dry-run rules as every mutating verb
    bxcachy init --print-answers          the saved answers

Exits: as `setup` (0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8); 4 also for no terminal without `--answers`. The wizard is only a front end: every answer becomes an ordinary command, so anything it does can be run by hand.

The login session follows the choice: `hyprland` starts Hyprland, `plasma` starts Plasma, and `both` asks (`login_session`, default Hyprland). `session set` runs for the resulting session. Databases: `db engine` remembers the container engine (`container_engine`), then `db start ENGINE` runs for each picked service (none is preselected); `database_passwords` (`generate` default: "Generated (recommended)", or `ask`: "My own password"; the question appears once a database is picked) adds `--ask-password` for the engines that have a password (the typed password is never stored in `answers.json`; asking needs a terminal, so a headless `init` with `ask` fails that step with exit 4). Apps: Basic runs `install --shell=...`; Customize runs one `install` with the ticked apps (filtered by desktop); then `default browser` and `default terminal`. Answers whose command does not exist yet (`ssh_key`; and `workspaces`, `natural_scroll`, `layouts`, `theme`, `wallpaper` when Hyprland is not being set up, because only the Hyprland starter takes them) are saved and listed as `pending`, never dropped silently. `init` at a terminal runs the wizard, saves `answers.json`, then runs the plan (the review screen is the confirmation; `--dry-run` only prints). `install.sh` ends with `bxcachy init` at a terminal and prints a hint otherwise.

### 14.4 Rules

* Every answer is optional; an unanswered page does nothing. The review screen lists exactly the commands that will run.
* `init` never runs a step the user did not choose, and never overwrites a file the user changed (the config service rules of section 6 apply).
* Starter configs are parametrized by the answers (workspaces, window style, layouts, theme, wallpaper, bar position, world clocks, natural scroll); the defaults are the current starters.
* Databases follow the earlier plan (`plan.md` section 7): Podman is the default engine and Docker is an explicit choice; services run as containers with start, stop, status and logs, persistent volumes and generated passwords kept in a mode-600 file.
* Runner integration (legacy `bxcachy-runner`): launcher providers `system`, `noctalia`, `rofi`, `walker`, `krunner`, `vicinae`, `hyprrunner`, `custom`; menu providers `rofi`, `walker`, `vicinae`, `hyprrunner`; commands are JSON argument arrays, never shell strings; keybindings are never changed. Default on Hyprland is Noctalia (Super+Space).
* The TUI needs MatchBox's `bif-tui` in the native runner (task W2). Until then `init --answers` is the only form.

title: Command reference
body: Command reference Every command is bxcachy NAME ... . This page is generated from docs/reference/cli.json ; the same data answers bxcachy help and bxcachy help NAME in the terminal. The command contract has the details behind each one. How commands behave Flag What it does --json Print one JSON object instead of text (see below). Every command takes it. --yes Apply a change that installs packages or edits system files. Without it you get the plan and exit code 2. --dry-run Print the plan or the exact commands and exit 0. Nothing is changed. --force Where it exists: replace a file BxCachy would otherwise keep because you edited it. Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar, the font) act at once and need no --yes . Exit codes Code Meaning 0 Done, or nothing to do (also --dry-run ). 1 A check came out negative (for example package-status says it is missing). 2 Usage error, or a plan was printed because --yes was not given. 3 Timeout, or the item is not available. 4 A precondition failed: not Arch or CachyOS, a tool or a monitor that is not there, an unknown name. 5 The official (pacman) phase failed. 6 The AUR phase, or the command you asked for, failed. 7 Partial success: some items were done, some failed. 8 Config conflict: a file you edited, or another run is in progress. 9 Internal error. 10 update check : an update is available. JSON { "schema": 1, "command": "dns", "version": "0.11.0", "ok": true, "exit": 0, "dry_run": false, "data": { }, "warnings": [] } data is different for every command; ok is true when exit is 0. Scripts should read exit and data , never the text. All commands Start here : init , wizard , status , doctor , update , version , menu , apps , help Install and remove : install , remove , pkg , catalog , plan , install-plan , optional-plan , profile-plan , profile-install-plan , profile-install , optional-install , profile-list , optional-list , desktop-list , tui-list , web-list , package-status , package-source , dev-plan , prerequisites , apps-doctor , web , toolchain Desktop setup : setup , session , tiling , plasma , keys , runner , default , layout , assets , config Look and feel : theme , appearance , display , power , time , toggle , nightshift , notify System and security : system , security , dns , kernel , ssh , secrets , vpn , cloud , settings , dotfiles , nas Develop : boxlang , editor , db , containers , vm , ai , skills Everyday tools : screenshot , qr , record , clipboard , emoji , forcequit , window , overview , quicklook , dolphin , dictation , strata , gpu , input , airplay Start here Set up the machine, see where it stands, keep it current. bxcachy init {#bxcachy-init} The setup wizard: asks the questions, shows a review, then runs the matching commands. bxcachy init [--from=FILE] [--fresh | --rerun] | init --answers=FILE [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] | init --print-answers [--from-system] [--json] | init --export=FILE [--force] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxcachy init bxcachy init --answers=answers.json --yes bxcachy init --print-answers --from-system --json bxcachy wizard {#bxcachy-wizard} Wizard pieces for scripts: render the demo screens or a pages file. bxcachy wizard --demo [--out=FILE] | --pages=FILE [--out=FILE] [--answers=FILE] bxcachy wizard --demo bxcachy status {#bxcachy-status} What is installed and configured on this machine, compared with what BxCachy would do. bxcachy status [--json] bxcachy status bxcachy status --json bxcachy doctor {#bxcachy-doctor} Checks the machine (Arch or CachyOS, pacman, sudo, disk) and reports problems. bxcachy doctor [--json] bxcachy doctor bxcachy update {#bxcachy-update} Check for a BxCachy update, apply it, pick a channel, turn the daily notification on or off. bxcachy update check [--notify] | apply [--yes] | channel [stable|beta] | notifications on|off|status [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxcachy update check bxcachy update apply --yes bxcachy update channel beta bxcachy update notifications on Exit 10 from update check means an update is available. bxcachy version {#bxcachy-version} The BxCachy version and build. bxcachy version [--json] bxcachy version bxcachy menu {#bxcachy-menu} The control center: every command as a menu on your launcher (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae). bxcachy menu | menu items [--json] | menu search TEXT [--json] bxcachy menu bxcachy menu search 'time zone' Bind it to a key; the first entry, Search, lists every entry as one flat list. bxcachy apps {#bxcachy-apps} Your installed catalog apps, as a list or a launcher grid. bxcachy apps | apps list [--json] bxcachy apps list bxcachy help {#bxcachy-help} This list, or the usage of one command. bxcachy help [COMMAND] bxcachy help bxcachy help appearance Install and remove Apps from the catalog, any package from the repositories or the AUR, and the reverse. bxcachy install {#bxcachy-install} Install catalog apps by id (or a whole group or profile). bxcachy install [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run] Changes the system: needs --yes . Without it you get the plan (exit 2); --dry-run shows it and exits 0. bxcachy install --dry-run bxcachy install --yes With no name it installs the default set; without --yes it prints the plan and changes nothing. bxcachy remove {#bxcachy-remove} Uninstall catalog apps (their packages or web launchers). bxcachy remove ID_OR_PACKAGE... [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] Changes the system: needs --yes . # Command reference

Every command is `bxcachy NAME ...`. This page is generated from `docs/reference/cli.json`; the same data answers `bxcachy help` and `bxcachy help NAME` in the terminal. The [command contract](/architecture/COMMAND-CONTRACT/index.html) has the details behind each one.

## How commands behave

|    Flag     |                                               What it does                                                |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--json`    | Print one JSON object instead of text (see below). Every command takes it.                                |
| `--yes`     | Apply a change that installs packages or edits system files. Without it you get the plan and exit code 2. |
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan or the exact commands and exit 0. Nothing is changed.                                      |
| `--force`   | Where it exists: replace a file BxCachy would otherwise keep because you edited it.                       |

Settings that only touch your own config (a theme, the bar, the font) act at once and need no `--yes`.

### Exit codes

| Code |                                               Meaning                                               |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0    | Done, or nothing to do (also `--dry-run`).                                                          |
| 1    | A check came out negative (for example `package-status` says it is missing).                        |
| 2    | Usage error, or a plan was printed because `--yes` was not given.                                   |
| 3    | Timeout, or the item is not available.                                                              |
| 4    | A precondition failed: not Arch or CachyOS, a tool or a monitor that is not there, an unknown name. |
| 5    | The official (pacman) phase failed.                                                                 |
| 6    | The AUR phase, or the command you asked for, failed.                                                |
| 7    | Partial success: some items were done, some failed.                                                 |
| 8    | Config conflict: a file you edited, or another run is in progress.                                  |
| 9    | Internal error.                                                                                     |
| 10   | `update check`: an update is available.                                                             |

### JSON

```json
{ "schema": 1, "command": "dns", "version": "0.11.0", "ok": true, "exit": 0, "dry_run": false, "data": { }, "warnings": [] }
```

`data` is different for every command; `ok` is true when `exit` is 0. Scripts should read `exit` and `data`, never the text.

## Install and remove

### `bxcachy install` {#bxcachy-install}

Install catalog apps by id (or a whole group or profile).

```text
bxcachy install [NAME] [--optional] [--shell=hyprland|plasma|all] [--json] [--yes] [--dry-run]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxcachy install --dry-run
bxcachy install --yes
```

> With no name it installs the default set; without --yes it prints the plan and changes nothing.

### `bxcachy remove` {#bxcachy-remove}

## Look and feel

### `bxcachy theme` {#bxcachy-theme}

```text
bxcachy theme list | show NAME | set NAME [--mode=theme|dark|light|auto] [--keep-wallpaper] | random | next | mode theme|dark|light|auto | install GIT_URL [--name=N] [--force] | import PATH [--name=N] [--force] | remove NAME | status [--dry-run] [--json]
```

### `bxcachy appearance` {#bxcachy-appearance}

Bar, dock, windows, animations, layout, fonts and backgrounds, one setting at a time.

```text
bxcachy appearance status|apply [--json]

bxcachy appearance dock show|hide|toggle | mode always|autohide|off | position bottom|left|right
```

## System and security

### `bxcachy system` {#bxcachy-system}

Update the system (a snapshot first), lock, suspend, log out, reboot, shut down.

```text
bxcachy system update [--yes] | lock | suspend | logout|reboot|shutdown [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxcachy system update --yes
bxcachy system reboot --yes
```

> lock and suspend act at once; logout, reboot and shutdown need --yes (the menu asks first).

### `bxcachy security` {#bxcachy-security}

Fingerprint and security key for sudo, SSH server, passwordless sudo, with guards.

```text
bxcachy security status [--json]

bxcachy security ssh-server on|off [--yes]
bxcachy security passwordless-sudo on|off [--yes]
```

Changes the system: needs `--yes`. Without it you get the plan (exit 2); `--dry-run` shows it and exits 0.

```bash
bxcachy security status
bxcachy security fingerprint on --dry-run
bxcachy security passwordless-sudo on --yes
```

> Only /etc/pam.d/sudo is ever changed, with a `sufficient` line and a backup; sudoers is checked with visudo first. `--dry-run` prints the exact line.

API keys and tokens in the system keyring, loaded per command, exported encrypted.

```text
bxcachy secrets status | setup [--keyring=kwallet|gnome-keyring|none] [--yes] | list [--type=ai|other] | set NAME [--from-file=F] [--type=ai|other] [--provider=ID] | get NAME [--show] | unset NAME --yes | apply [--yes] | global on NAME --yes|off NAME|show | unlock | lock | export FILE [--plain] [--force] --yes | import FILE [--overwrite] --yes | env [NAMES...] | run [NAMES...] [--strict] -- COMMAND [ARGS...] [--json]
```

```text
bxcachy nas auto on|off NAME SHARE [--yes]
```

markdown:
# BxCachy

**BxCachy** turns a fresh CachyOS install into a finished developer machine: Hyprland with Noctalia (KDE Plasma stays installed beside it), BoxLang and MatchBox, your apps, your shell, your AI agents, all chosen in one guided setup. It is a single native program written in [BoxLang](https://boxlang.io) and compiled with [MatchBox](https://matchbox.boxlang.io).

*This is the documentation for version 1.0.x.*

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash
```

It checks your machine, downloads and verifies the release, installs everything, then starts the setup wizard. See [Getting started](/getting-started/index.html).

## What you get

Hyprland and Noctalia, or Plasma with tiling and a status panel. Mac-style keys, screenshots, notifications, night shift.

The control center: search every setting, install any package, change the look, monitors, power, time zone and DNS.

A curated catalog of 280 apps and web apps, with one-click Google, Microsoft and Apple suites.

BoxLang, MatchBox, their version managers, VS Code with the extension, and modules from ForgeBox.

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and more, with keys in your keyring and skills that teach them BxCachy.

## How it behaves

* Nothing changes until you say so: every command prints a plan and needs `--yes`.
* Files you edit are kept. BxCachy only rewrites files it wrote itself.
* Everything is also a command, with `--json` output, so you can script it.

# The setup wizard

`bxcachy init` opens a full-screen form with these pages: **Desktop** , **Look** , **Input** , **Developer** , **Toolchains** , **Containers** , **Apps** , **AI** , **Extras** and **Import**, then a review screen that lists exactly the commands it will run. Nothing runs until you confirm.

## Run it again

On a machine that is already set up the wizard starts from your saved answers plus what it finds on the system, and marks installed options with `✓ installed`.

|          Command           |                    Starts from                    |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `bxcachy init`             | your saved answers and what the system has (tune) |
| `bxcachy init --rerun`     | your saved answers only                           |
| `bxcachy init --fresh`     | the defaults                                      |
| `bxcachy init --from FILE` | an answers file from another machine              |

Nothing the machine already has is ever removed. `bxcachy status` shows the same scan without opening the wizard.

## Without a terminal

```bash
bxcachy init --answers answers.json --yes     # apply an answers file
bxcachy init --defaults --yes                  # the wizard's default answers
bxcachy init --dry-run                         # show the plan only
bxcachy init --export answers.json             # save your answers for another machine
```

Answers are saved in `~/.config/bxcachy/answers.json` (mode 600). They never contain secrets.

## Defaults worth knowing

|   Question   |                       Default                       |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Desktop      | Hyprland + Noctalia                                 |
| Workspaces   | 4                                                   |
| Shell        | zsh with the Starship prompt (Catppuccin Powerline) |
| Terminal     | Ghostty                                             |
| File manager | Strata                                              |
| Toolchains   | Java and Rust                                       |
| Containers   | Podman (with `docker` commands mapped to it)        |
| Dictation    | Superwhisper (Voxtype is the alternative)           |
| Updates      | stable channel, daily notification                  |

markdown:
# Getting started

## What you need

* CachyOS (or another Arch-based system with `pacman`), x86_64.
* A normal user with `sudo`. The installer refuses to run as root.
* A network connection.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash
```

The installer:

1. checks the machine;
2. downloads the program and the install bundle for your [channel](/guides/updates/index.html) and verifies their signature and SHA-256;
3. installs packages, toolchains (Java 21, `bvm`, `mvm`, BoxLang, MatchBox, Rust) and the core apps;
4. starts the [setup wizard](/guides/wizard/index.html).

Its log is `~/.cache/bxcachy/install.log`.

### Without anyone at the keyboard

```bash
curl -fsSL {{ installUrl }} | bash -s -- --yes --answers answers.json
```

`--yes` never asks (it needs passwordless sudo). Without `--answers`, the wizard's default answers are applied. More options: `--channel stable|beta`, `--no-wizard`, `--dry-run`.

## After the install

|         Do this         |               With                |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| See what is set up      | `bxcachy status`                  |
| Change your choices     | `bxcachy init`                    |
| Open the control center | `Super+Alt+M` or `bxcachy menu`   |
| See every shortcut      | `Super+K` or `bxcachy keys sheet` |
| Check for updates       | `bxcachy update check`            |

New to BoxLang? Run `bxcachy boxlang welcome` for a getting-started page, or open [Try BoxLang](https://try.boxlang.io).

title: MatchBox parity
body: MatchBox parity work: class entry, mappings, Application.bx Source of truth: BoxLang JVM ( ortus-boxlang/boxlang , read 2026-11-09 at b8ea0f0) and the BoxLang docs (CLI Scripting, Application.bx). MatchBox today (develop + our PRs) supports none of the three for scripts or native builds. 1. Class as entry point ( boxlang Task.bx a b ) JVM: BoxRuntime.executeTemplate sends .bx / .cfc files to executeClass . A request context is created and the Application listener is resolved (section 3). The class is instantiated (its init is NOT special here; the constructor runs, pseudo-constructor included). If the instance has a main member ( this scope), run listener.onRequestStart(templatePath) . If it returns true, call main( args ) where args is an array of the raw CLI arguments after the file name , in order ( ["hola", "--many", "options=test"] ). main may be an instance or static method; args = [] default is the convention. Errors: abort -> onAbort ; missing include -> onMissingTemplate ; any other exception -> log, then onError(exception, "") , rethrown if onError is false. Always onRequestEnd(templatePath) and flush output. No main : error Class [X] does not have a main method to execute. (non-zero exit). A path without extension is presumed to be <path>.bx . CLIGetArgs() and server.cli.parsed work inside the class as in scripts. 2. Mappings The only ways to declare them (owner decision, matches the JVM): this.mappings in Application.bx . mappings in boxlang.json (runtime config; the JVM default is { "/": "${user-dir}" } ). The bx:application component, which merges all of its attributes into the application settings ( name , mappings , ...), then recomputes the request config. Value forms: a string path, or a struct { path, external } ( path required, external default true ; BoxLang 1.6+). Names are normalized to a leading and trailing slash ( models and /models/ are the same). Application mappings are merged over the global ones, application wins. Class resolution order ( BoxResolver.findFromLocal ): 1) relative to the current template, 2) mappings (a mapping matches when the class path, as a slash path, starts with the mapping name; one candidate per valid extension, .bx before .bxs as configured), 3) custom component/class paths. Applies to new , import , extends , implements and createObject("class", name) . 3. Application.bx for scripts and classes Discovery ( ApplicationService.loadDescriptorTemplate ): for an absolute script path, the descriptor is looked up in the script's directory only ; for non-absolute (mapped) paths it walks up from the template's directory to its mapping root. markdown:
# MatchBox parity work: class entry, mappings, Application.bx

Source of truth: BoxLang JVM (`ortus-boxlang/boxlang`, read 2026-11-09 at b8ea0f0) and the BoxLang docs (CLI Scripting, Application.bx). MatchBox today (develop + our PRs) supports none of the three for scripts or native builds.

## 1. Class as entry point (`boxlang Task.bx a b`)

JVM: `BoxRuntime.executeTemplate` sends `.bx`/`.cfc` files to `executeClass`.

1. A request context is created and the Application listener is resolved (section 3).
2. The class is instantiated (its `init` is NOT special here; the constructor runs, pseudo-constructor included).
3. If the instance has a `main` member (`this` scope), run `listener.onRequestStart(templatePath)`. If it returns true, call `main( args )` where `args` is an **array of the raw CLI arguments after the file name** , in order (`["hola", "--many", "options=test"]`). `main` may be an instance or static method; `args = []` default is the convention.
4. Errors: abort -\> `onAbort`; missing include -\> `onMissingTemplate`; any other exception -\> log, then `onError(exception, "")`, rethrown if `onError` is false. Always `onRequestEnd(templatePath)` and flush output.
5. No `main`: error `Class [X] does not have a main method to execute.` (non-zero exit).
6. A path without extension is presumed to be `<path>.bx`. `CLIGetArgs()` and `server.cli.parsed` work inside the class as in scripts.

## 2. Mappings

The only ways to declare them (owner decision, matches the JVM):

* `this.mappings` in `Application.bx`.
* `mappings` in `boxlang.json` (runtime config; the JVM default is `{ "/": "${user-dir}" }`).
* The `bx:application` component, which merges all of its attributes into the application settings (`name`, `mappings`, ...), then recomputes the request config.

Value forms: a string path, or a struct `{ path, external }` (`path` required, `external` default `true`; BoxLang 1.6+). Names are normalized to a leading and trailing slash (`models` and `/models/` are the same). Application mappings are merged over the global ones, application wins.

Class resolution order (`BoxResolver.findFromLocal`): 1) relative to the current template, 2) mappings (a mapping matches when the class path, as a slash path, starts with the mapping name; one candidate per valid extension, `.bx` before `.bxs` as configured), 3) custom component/class paths. Applies to `new`, `import`, `extends`, `implements` and `createObject("class", name)`.

## 3. Application.bx for scripts and classes

Discovery (`ApplicationService.loadDescriptorTemplate`): for an absolute script path, the descriptor is looked up in **the script's directory only** ; for non-absolute (mapped) paths it walks up from the template's directory to its mapping root. Lookup order in a directory: class files `Application.bx` (valid class extensions, then `.cfc`), then templates `Application.<template extension>`. The class is instantiated **without calling `init()`**.

Settings read from `this`: `name`, `mappings`, `datasource`/`defaultDatasource`/`datasources`, `javaSettings`, `classPaths`/`componentPaths`, `customComponentPaths`, `caches`, `schedulers`, `watchers`, `timezone`, `locale`, `runtimeSettings`, security extension lists. A settings change recomputes the request config.

Lifecycle for a script or class run (no web scopes): application defined on first use -\> `onApplicationStart()` once (only if `this.name` is set; false aborts) -\> `onRequestStart(targetPage)` (false aborts) -\> run the script (`template.invoke`; `onRequest` is not used for scripts) or `main(args)` -\> `onRequestEnd()` -\> flush. Errors go to `onError(exception, eventName)`; `abort` to `onAbort(targetPage)`. `onApplicationEnd(applicationScope)` on shutdown. Session hooks never fire in CLI.

## 4. Order of MatchBox work

1. Class entry with `main(args)` (interpreter and native).
2. Mappings: `boxlang.json`/`matchbox.toml` mappings plus `this.mappings` read from `Application.bx`; resolution wired into `new`, `import`, `extends`, `createObject`.
3. Application.bx for scripts and classes, with the lifecycle above.

Native builds resolve classes at compile time, so mapped directories must exist when `matchbox --target native` runs; the Application.bx settings that affect compilation (mappings) are read at build time, and the lifecycle runs inside the binary.

## MatchBox VM fixes (PRs 156 to 160, in the `bxcachy` branch)

Found while building the installer, fixed upstream, and BxCachy no longer works around them: `break` in nested for-in loops (#156), a broken pipe on stdout (#157), calling a function stored in `variables` (#158), `switch` with `var` slots and the default jump (#159), and the panic message that was hidden (#160). Behaviour change in #159: a `var` declared in one `case` is not visible in another case.

# The control center

`bxcachy menu` (bound to `Super+Alt+M`) opens a menu on your launcher (Rofi, Walker, Wofi, Fuzzel or Vicinae: `bxcachy runner set NAME`). It follows Omarchy's layout and adds a Develop section for what is ours.

|       Section        |                                                               What is in it                                                                |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Search               | Every entry of the menu as one flat list; type to filter, press Enter to run it.                                                           |
| Apps                 | Your installed apps.                                                                                                                       |
| Install              | Any package from the repositories or the AUR, the catalog by group (AI, Development, Terminal, Gaming), web apps, virtual machines, fonts. |
| Remove               | Packages, catalog apps, web apps, themes, virtual machines, agent skills. It asks first.                                                   |
| Appearance           | Theme, mode, font, background, bar, dock, windows, animations. See [Appearance](/guides/appearance/index.html).                            |
| Trigger              | Screenshots and recording, toggles (do not disturb, stay awake, night light), emoji, clipboard history, force quit, overview.              |
| Setup                | Power, Display, Defaults, Keyboard, Security, Time, DNS, Kernel, Cloud storage, Hardware.                                                  |
| Update               | BxCachy updates, the system update (a snapshot first), skills, re-apply appearance and display.                                            |
| Develop              | BoxLang, databases, virtual machines, containers, the editor.                                                                              |
| Agent                | Open an agent, the pull-down AI shell, sessions, local models, API keys.                                                                   |
| Learn, About, System | Docs and cheat sheets, the status of this machine, lock, suspend, log out, reboot, shut down.                                              |

Every entry is a command you can type: `bxcachy menu items` lists them with the command each one runs, and `bxcachy menu search TEXT` finds one. Entries that print something open in a terminal and wait for Enter; entries that need a choice (a theme, a font, a time zone, a monitor) ask you in the same menu.

# The desktop

BxCachy sets up **Hyprland with Noctalia** as the main desktop. **KDE Plasma** stays installed and gets tiling and a status panel; pick either (or both) at the login screen (`bxcachy session set hyprland|plasma`).

## Hyprland and Noctalia

`bxcachy setup hyprland` installs the packages one by one and writes the starter configuration once. `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` is yours. BxCachy owns `~/.config/hypr/bxcachy.lua`, which it regenerates from the [shortcut table](/guides/shortcuts/index.html); never edit that file by hand.

## KDE Plasma

* **Tiling:** `bxcachy setup plasma` installs HyprKwin. Layouts: dwindle, master, monocle, scrolling, stage. `bxcachy tiling on|off|status|layout NAME`.
* **Panels:** `bxcachy plasma panels apply` replaces your panels with a top status panel (launcher, workspace pager, active window, clock, weather, media, system vitals, tray, in rounded islands with Panel Colorizer) and a bottom dock. Your old layout is backed up first: `bxcachy plasma panels undo --yes` restores it. From Hyprland it is applied at your next Plasma login.
* **Virtual desktops:** `bxcachy plasma desktops 4`.

Look and hardware have their own pages: [Appearance](/guides/appearance/index.html) for the bar, dock, windows and fonts, and [Displays, power and time](/guides/system/index.html) for monitors, laptop power and the time zone. The [control center](/guides/menu/index.html) has all of it as one menu.

## Everyday tools

|          Do          |                     Command                      |              Shortcut              |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Control center       | `bxcachy menu`                                   | `Super+Alt+M`                      |
| All apps window      | `bxcachy apps`                                   | `Super+Alt+Space`                  |
| Screenshot           | `bxcachy screenshot screen\|region\|window`      | `Super+Shift+3` / `4` / `5` (menu) |
| Text from the screen | `bxcachy screenshot ocr`                         | in the `5` menu                    |
| QR codes             | `bxcachy screenshot qr`, `bxcachy qr TEXT`       |                                    |
| Record the screen    | `bxcachy record toggle [--region]`               | `Super+Shift+R`                    |
| Clipboard history    | `bxcachy clipboard pick`                         | `Super+Shift+V`                    |
| Do Not Disturb       | `bxcachy notify dnd toggle`, `notify snooze 30m` | `Super+Alt+N`                      |
| Night shift          | `bxcachy nightshift on\|off\|toggle`             | `Super+Alt+Shift+N`                |
| Emoji                | `bxcachy emoji`                                  | `Super+Ctrl+E`                     |
| Force quit           | `bxcachy forcequit`                              | `Super+Alt+Escape`                 |
| Overview             | `bxcachy overview`                               | `Super+Ctrl+Up`                    |
| Minimize / restore   | `bxcachy window minimize\|restore`               | `Super+M` / `Super+Shift+M`        |
| Pull-down AI shell   | `bxcachy ai shell`                               | ``Super+```                        |

Night shift on Hyprland runs `wlsunset` with your time zone's sunrise and sunset (no network lookup); on Plasma it turns on Plasma's own Night Light.

## Trackpads and Apple devices

`bxcachy input gestures --yes` sets up three-finger swipes (workspaces, overview) with `libinput-gestures`. `bxcachy input doctor` checks Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad support (the kernel driver, Bluetooth, the `input` group). For Option-key characters like a Mac, pick the **English (US, Macintosh)** keyboard layout in the wizard. `bxcachy airplay on` starts an AirPlay receiver.

## Hot corners

Hot corners are left to you: on Plasma use System Settings → Screen Edges.

# Appearance

`bxcachy appearance` changes how the shell and the windows look. Each change acts at once, is remembered, and can be shown first with `--dry-run`. For colors, see [Themes](/guides/themes/index.html).

```bash
bxcachy appearance status
bxcachy appearance bar position bottom      # top, bottom, left, right
bxcachy appearance bar style glassy         # opaque, glassy, clear
bxcachy appearance bar clock iso            # ten clock formats (time-24h, sunday-12h, date-24h, iso ...)
bxcachy appearance bar battery on           # the percentage next to the battery
bxcachy appearance dock mode autohide       # always, autohide, off
bxcachy appearance windows gaps off         # no gaps and no borders
bxcachy appearance windows corners sharp    # theme, rounded, sharp
bxcachy appearance windows opacity glassy   # opaque, glassy
bxcachy appearance animations off
bxcachy appearance layout scrolling         # dwindle, scrolling, floating
bxcachy appearance font list
bxcachy appearance font install cascadia --yes
bxcachy appearance font cascadia            # Noctalia and the terminals follow
bxcachy appearance background random        # or: list, set NAME, next
bxcachy appearance apply                    # push everything you chose again
```

## Where the changes go

* **Noctalia** (bar, dock, clock, battery, font, corner radius) is changed with `noctalia msg config-set`, so your `config.toml` is not edited. Without Noctalia the choice is saved and `appearance apply` pushes it later.
* **Hyprland** window looks (gaps, corners, opacity, animations, layout) are one generated file, `~/.config/bxcachy/theme/look.lua`, loaded by `bxcachy.lua`. BxCachy reloads Hyprland after a change. Your own `hyprland.lua` is never touched.
* **Fonts** come from seven Nerd Fonts. Changing the font also updates the terminal configs BxCachy wrote, but never one you edited (it tells you which).
* **Backgrounds** are read from `~/Pictures/BxCachy`, `~/Pictures` and the current theme's folder.

The menu has all of this under Appearance.

# Shortcuts and Mac keys

BxCachy keeps one shortcut table and renders it for xremap (Cmd-style keys, on both desktops), the Hyprland module and Plasma. Press `Super+K` (or run `bxcachy keys sheet`) to see every shortcut in your menu program.

## Cmd-style keys

With Mac keys on, the Super key works like Cmd in apps: `Super+C V X Z A S F T N O P R W L B I U` and `Super+,` send the Ctrl version. In terminals `Super+C/V` copy and paste with `Ctrl+Shift`, `Super+T/N/W/F` become `Ctrl+Shift+T/N/W/F`, and the shell keys (`Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+A`...) are left alone. `bxcachy keys mac on|off` toggles it.

## Change a shortcut

```bash
bxcachy keys show                         # the table
bxcachy keys set control-center Super+Alt+C --yes
bxcachy keys reset control-center --yes
bxcachy keys conflicts                    # clashes with your own hyprland.lua
```

Your changes live in `~/.config/bxcachy/shortcuts.json`. Remaps (the Cmd keys) are xremap's and cannot be changed this way.

## The main ones

|            Keys             |                Does                |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `Super+Alt+M`               | Control center                     |
| `Super+Alt+Space`           | All apps                           |
| `Super+K`                   | Shortcut cheat sheet               |
| `Super+Shift+3` / `4` / `5` | Screenshot: screen / region / menu |
| `Super+Shift+R`             | Screen recording                   |
| `Super+Shift+V`             | Clipboard history                  |
| `Super+Ctrl+E`              | Emoji                              |
| `Super+Ctrl+X`              | Dictation on or off (Voxtype)      |
| `Super+Alt+N`               | Do Not Disturb                     |
| `Super+Q`                   | Close window                       |
| `Super+M` / `Super+Shift+M` | Minimize / show minimized          |

body: The setup wizard The BxCachy setup wizard: a full-screen terminal form written in BoxLang on MatchBox's terminal canvas ( docs/tui.md in the MatchBox repo). It draws pages given as JSON and writes the answers as JSON. It runs nothing itself; bxcachy init starts it and acts on the answers (COMMAND-CONTRACT.md section 14). bxcachy wizard --pages=pages.json --out=answers.json [--answers=saved.json] bxcachy wizard --demo [--out=answers.json] # built-in pages, to try it Exit codes: 0 answers written, 130 cancelled (nothing written), 2 usage, 4 unreadable pages or answers file. Pages { "title": "BxCachy", "tagline": "...", "version": "0.12.0", "pages": [ { "id": "desktop", "title": "Desktop", "intro": "...", "questions": [ { "type": "choice", "id": "desktops", "label": "...", "help": "...", "default": "both", "options": [ { "value": "hyprland", "label": "Hyprland", "description": "shown under the list when focused", "group": "optional heading" } ] }, { "type": "multi", "id": "layouts", "label": "...", "default": ["us"], "options": [ ... ] }, { "type": "text", "id": "git_name", "label": "...", "placeholder": "...", "default": "" }, { "type": "number", "id": "workspaces", "label": "...", "min": 1, "max": 10, "default": 2 }, { "type": "confirm", "id": "natural_scroll", "label": "...", "default": false }, { "type": "info", "label": "...", "help": "..." } ] } ] } Any question may carry "when": { "id": "other_question", "in": ["a", "b"] } (or "equals": "a" ): it is shown only while that answer matches, and a hidden question is left out of the review and the answers file. A whole page may carry when too: it is then skipped by Next and Back and left out of the sidebar, the step count, the review and the result. bxcachy init adds one page per catalog group after the Apps page this way (see AppPages ), shown only for "Customize". Answers are a flat JSON object keyed by question id: a string (choice, text), an array of strings (multi), a number, or a bool. Keys and mouse Up/Down (or j/k) move, Space selects or toggles, Enter finishes the question and moves on, Left/Right change a number, Tab/PageDown next page, Esc/Shift-Tab/PageUp previous page, Ctrl-C cancels. Clicks select options and jump to visited steps. Text fields take typing directly (Backspace deletes, Ctrl-U clears). Look Catppuccin Frappe neutrals with the Ortus brand gradient (cyan #00DBFF to green #00FF78 ), true colour, a fade-in between screens and a soft shimmer. The splash uses the official BoxLang icon as half-block pixel art ( assets/wizard/art-*.txt , embedded by bootstrap/gen-wizard.sh into src/bxcachy/WizardData.bx ). Every screen shows "Powered by BoxLang / www.boxlang.io ". It needs a 76x24 terminal; larger is nicer. Code Class Does WizardApp State and key handling, no drawing (unit tested). WizardView Draws a frame on the canvas and records click regions; testable with tui.render_to_string . Wizard The run loop: events in, frames out. WizardData Generated: demo pages and splash art. Developing Needs MatchBox built with bif-tui . (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_app_test.bxs) # logic (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_view_test.bxs) # what each screen shows bash tests/wizard-test.sh BXCACHY_NATIVE # end to end in a pseudo-terminal python3 tools/record-wizard.py --bin BXCACHY_NATIVE --out /tmp/rec # mp4 and gif (needs Pillow, pyte, ffmpeg)

# The setup wizard

The BxCachy setup wizard: a full-screen terminal form written in BoxLang on MatchBox's terminal canvas (`docs/tui.md` in the MatchBox repo). It draws pages given as
JSON and writes the answers as JSON. It runs nothing itself; `bxcachy init` starts it and acts on the answers
(COMMAND-CONTRACT.md section 14).

    bxcachy wizard --pages=pages.json --out=answers.json [--answers=saved.json]
    bxcachy wizard --demo [--out=answers.json]        # built-in pages, to try it

Exit codes: 0 answers written, 130 cancelled (nothing written), 2 usage, 4 unreadable pages or answers file.

## Pages

```json

  "pages": [ { "id": "desktop", "title": "Desktop", "intro": "...",
    "questions": [
      { "type": "choice",  "id": "desktops", "label": "...", "help": "...", "default": "both",
        "options": [ { "value": "hyprland", "label": "Hyprland", "description": "shown under the list when focused", "group": "optional heading" } ] },
      { "type": "multi",   "id": "layouts",  "label": "...", "default": ["us"], "options": [ ... ] },
      { "type": "text",    "id": "git_name", "label": "...", "placeholder": "...", "default": "" },
      { "type": "number",  "id": "workspaces", "label": "...", "min": 1, "max": 10, "default": 2 },
      { "type": "confirm", "id": "natural_scroll", "label": "...", "default": false },
      { "type": "info",    "label": "...", "help": "..." } ] } ] }
```

Any question may carry `"when": { "id": "other_question", "in": ["a", "b"] }` (or `"equals": "a"`): it is shown only while that answer matches, and a hidden question is left out of the review and the answers file.

A whole page may carry `when` too: it is then skipped by Next and Back and left out of the sidebar, the step count, the review and the result. `bxcachy init` adds one page per catalog group after the Apps page this way (see `AppPages`), shown only for "Customize".

Answers are a flat JSON object keyed by question id: a string (choice, text), an array of strings (multi), a number, or a bool.

## Keys and mouse

Up/Down (or j/k) move, Space selects or toggles, Enter finishes the question and moves on, Left/Right change a number,
Tab/PageDown next page, Esc/Shift-Tab/PageUp previous page, Ctrl-C cancels. Clicks select options and jump to visited steps.
Text fields take typing directly (Backspace deletes, Ctrl-U clears).

## Look

Catppuccin Frappe neutrals with the Ortus brand gradient (cyan `#00DBFF` to green `#00FF78`), true colour, a fade-in between
screens and a soft shimmer. The splash uses the official BoxLang icon as half-block pixel art (`assets/wizard/art-*.txt`, embedded by `bootstrap/gen-wizard.sh` into `src/bxcachy/WizardData.bx`). Every screen shows "Powered by BoxLang / [www.boxlang.io](http://www.boxlang.io)". It needs a 76x24 terminal; larger is nicer.

## Code

|    Class     |                                             Does                                             |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `WizardApp`  | State and key handling, no drawing (unit tested).                                            |
| `WizardView` | Draws a frame on the canvas and records click regions; testable with `tui.render_to_string`. |
| `Wizard`     | The run loop: events in, frames out.                                                         |
| `WizardData` | Generated: demo pages and splash art.                                                        |

## Developing

Needs MatchBox built with `bif-tui`.

    (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_app_test.bxs)    # logic
    (cd src && matchbox ../tests/wizard_view_test.bxs)   # what each screen shows
    bash tests/wizard-test.sh BXCACHY_NATIVE             # end to end in a pseudo-terminal
    python3 tools/record-wizard.py --bin BXCACHY_NATIVE --out /tmp/rec   # mp4 and gif (needs Pillow, pyte, ffmpeg)

markdown:
# Themes

BxCachy ships 15 color themes in the Omarchy theme format: five of ours and ten taken from Omarchy.

```bash
bxcachy theme list                  # all themes, the current one marked
bxcachy theme set tokyo-night       # apply one now
bxcachy theme next                  # or random
bxcachy theme mode auto             # theme, dark, light or auto
bxcachy theme status
```

Setting a theme acts at once. `--dry-run` shows what would be written without changing anything.

## What changes

|                      Where                      |                                       How                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Noctalia (bar, launcher, panels, notifications) | a generated palette and the light or dark mode                                  |
| Ghostty, kitty, alacritty, foot                 | generated files that the starter configs include                                |
| btop                                            | a generated theme file                                                          |
| Hyprland window borders                         | the accent color, read by the managed `bxcachy.lua`                             |
| Neovim (LazyVim setup)                          | the matching colorscheme, applied live without a restart                        |
| KDE Plasma                                      | switches between Breeze Light and Breeze Dark                                   |
| Wallpaper                                       | a BxCachy theme brings one of our wallpapers; use `--keep-wallpaper` to skip it |

Not themed: the Starship prompt, VS Code, browsers and GTK or Qt apps. Your own config files are never edited. Terminal configs you wrote yourself need one include line, which `bxcachy theme set` prints.

Bar, dock, windows, fonts and backgrounds are in [Appearance](/guides/appearance/index.html).

## The themes

BxCachy, BxCachy Light, BxCachy Midnight, BxCachy Cyan and BxCachy Forest are ours. From Omarchy: catppuccin, catppuccin-latte, tokyo-night, gruvbox, nord, rose-pine, kanagawa, everforest, matte-black and flexoki-light (MIT, credited in `themes/NOTICE.md`).

## More themes, and your own

`bxcachy theme install https://github.com/someone/omarchy-name-theme` installs an Omarchy-style theme repository (https only). Themes you already have in `~/.config/omarchy/themes` are found automatically. A theme is a folder with `colors.toml`, an optional `neovim.lua` and an optional `backgrounds/` folder:

```bash
bxcachy theme import ~/my-theme --name=mine
bxcachy theme remove mine
```

Both `colors.toml` formats are understood: the named colors of current Omarchy and the older `color0` to `color15` list.

## Neovim

`bxcachy editor lazyvim --yes` installs the LazyVim starter plus the BxCachy layer: transparent background, BoxLang syntax highlighting ([vim-boxlang](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/vim-boxlang)), no news popups, the neo-tree extra, and live theme following. An existing `~/.config/nvim` is never touched. To add only BoxLang syntax to a LazyVim config you already have: `bxcachy editor boxlang --yes`.

## The BoxLang prompt segment

The starter Starship prompt shows your BoxLang version, like Java, in folders with `.bx`, `.bxs`, `.bxm`, `.cfc`, `.cfm` or `.cfs` files, `box.json` or `Application.bx`. The starter file is written once, so an existing prompt keeps what you have; `bxcachy config diff starship` shows what is new.

# Apps and web apps

## The catalog

BxCachy knows about 280 apps and web apps in groups (development, terminal, AI, infrastructure, network, system, desktop, everyday, web apps, media, gaming). Each is **default** (installed by the wizard's Basic mode) or **optional** . Sources: official packages first (`pacman`), then the AUR (`yay`), Omarchy's packages, vendor installers and web apps.

```bash
bxcachy catalog list --group media
bxcachy catalog show strata
bxcachy install vlc heidisql --yes
bxcachy profile-install jvm --yes        # a ready-made set
```

In the wizard, **Basic** installs the recommended set; **Customize** lets you tick apps per category. Some entries only apply to one desktop (they say so).

## Web apps

A web app is a frameless window with its own launcher entry.

```bash
bxcachy web add Notion https://notion.so --yes
bxcachy web list
bxcachy web install google --yes         # Docs, Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube...
bxcachy web install microsoft --yes      # Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive
bxcachy web install apple --yes          # iCloud, Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Apple Music, Apple TV
```

The same three are in the wizard (Apps page) and the control center (Web apps).

## Defaults

```bash
bxcachy default show
bxcachy default browser brave --yes
bxcachy default terminal ghostty --yes
bxcachy default filemanager strata --yes
```

## Files and sharing

The default file manager is **Strata** ; Dolphin is the alternative (`bxcachy dolphin doctor` checks it works outside Plasma). `bxcachy strata integrations` adds LocalSend and KDE Connect to Strata's *Send to* menu. `bxcachy quicklook PATH` previews a file with Kiview.

## More

|           Area           |                                                   Command                                                   |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Dictation                | `bxcachy dictation setup superwhisper\|voxtype --yes`                                                       |
| Databases                | `bxcachy db list\|start ENGINE\|stop\|status\|logs` (Podman first; HeidiSQL and DBeaver are in the catalog) |
| Cloud storage as folders | `bxcachy cloud remotes\|configure\|mount NAME\|status` (RClone Browser is the GUI)                          |
| VPN                      | `bxcachy vpn nordvpn setup`                                                                                 |
| Containers               | `bxcachy containers doctor\|socket enable\|docker-compat`                                                   |
| Editor                   | `bxcachy editor lazyvim`                                                                                    |
| GPU drivers              | `bxcachy gpu doctor`                                                                                        |

markdown:
# Displays, power and time

## Displays

```bash
bxcachy display list
bxcachy display scale DP-2 1.5          # auto or 0.5 to 4
bxcachy display rotate DP-2 90
bxcachy display mode DP-2 2560x1440@144
bxcachy display position DP-2 2880x0
bxcachy display mirror on               # the laptop panel on every external monitor
bxcachy display laptop off              # refused when no other monitor would be on
bxcachy display brightness up           # down, or set 40
bxcachy display apply                   # push what is saved again
```

On Hyprland the settings are one generated file, `~/.config/bxcachy/theme/monitors.lua`, loaded after your own `hyprland.lua`, and Hyprland reloads. On Plasma they go through `kscreen-doctor`.

## Laptop power

CachyOS does not ship laptop power tools, so BxCachy adds them.

```bash
bxcachy power status
bxcachy power setup --yes               # power-profiles-daemon and upower; nothing happens on a desktop
bxcachy power profile saver             # performance, balanced, saver
bxcachy power lid lock --yes            # suspend, lock or ignore when the lid closes
bxcachy power doctor                    # daemons, the lid, zram, swap for hibernation
```

The lid setting is a logind drop-in and applies from the next login. Hibernation is not configured for you; `doctor` tells you whether your swap is big enough.

## Time zone and travel

```bash
bxcachy time status
bxcachy time zone Europe/Madrid --yes   # set it (bxcachy time zone --list shows them all)
bxcachy time sync --yes                 # after you land: set the zone from your IP address
bxcachy time auto on --yes              # or follow your location by itself
bxcachy time ntp on --yes
```

`time auto on` installs GeoClue and `automatic-timezoned`, writes the service and the GeoClue settings it needs, and enables it. **GeoClue looks your location up online (the Wi-Fi networks around you or your IP address)** , so the plan says so before you agree. `time auto off` removes everything it wrote. If the zone does not follow you, read `journalctl -u automatic-timezoned`.

## DNS, kernels and stay awake

```bash
bxcachy dns                              # the servers in use
bxcachy dns cloudflare --yes             # google, quad9, custom 9.9.9.10, dhcp
bxcachy kernel list
bxcachy kernel install linux-cachyos-lts --yes
bxcachy toggle stay-awake                # keep the screen from idling (Noctalia)
```

`dns` changes the active NetworkManager connections. `kernel` installs or removes kernel packages with their headers; it never edits the bootloader, never removes the running or the last kernel, and you pick the kernel in the boot menu. Stay awake needs Noctalia (Hyprland); on Plasma use System Settings.

markdown:
# Virtual machines

`bxcachy vm` runs full desktops in containers: Windows (the dockur/windows image) and Linux desktops (LinuxServer's webtop, a desktop in your browser). They use Podman, or Docker if you chose it with `bxcachy db engine docker`.

```bash
bxcachy vm doctor                          # is this machine ready? (KVM, groups, GPU, disk)
bxcachy vm create linux dev                # a Ubuntu XFCE desktop called dev
bxcachy vm create linux arch --tag=arch-kde --gpu=auto
bxcachy vm create windows                  # asks which Windows
bxcachy vm list                            # all of them: state, ports, disk used
bxcachy vm open dev                        # starts it if needed and opens it
```

`create` shows a plan first; add `--yes` to do it. `--dry-run` never changes anything.

## Linux desktops

`bxcachy vm versions linux` lists the tags: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch with XFCE, KDE Plasma, MATE or i3 (plus LXQt on Ubuntu), and a small Alpine. The default is `ubuntu-xfce`. Make as many as you want; each gets its own port, data folder and password.

`vm open NAME` opens `https://127.0.0.1:PORT/` in your browser. The certificate is self-signed, so accept it once. The user is `bxcachy`; show the password with `bxcachy vm info NAME --show-password`.

**GPU** (optional): `--gpu=intel` or `--gpu=amd` passes `/dev/dri` in. `--gpu=nvidia` is supported too; it needs the NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and the NVIDIA container toolkit, and it is not available on the Alpine tags. `--gpu=auto` uses `/dev/dri` when the machine has it. `vm doctor` shows what your machine has.

## Windows

You pick the version when you create it:

|            Choice             |    Size     |                         Note                          |
|-------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `11` Windows 11 Pro           | 7.9 GB      | the usual choice                                      |
| `11l` Windows 11 LTSC         | 4.7 GB      | long-term servicing edition, fewer bundled apps       |
| `11e` Windows 11 Enterprise   | 6.6 GB      | business edition                                      |
| `10` Windows 10 Pro           | 5.7 GB      | older, for legacy needs                               |
| `10l` Windows 10 LTSC         | 4.6 GB      | long-term servicing edition                           |
| `tiny11` Tiny11               | 5.3 GB      | **unofficial** stripped-down build from the community |
| `core11` Tiny11 Core          | 3.0 GB      | **unofficial**, the most stripped-down                |
| `tiny10` Tiny10               | 3.6 GB      | **unofficial** stripped-down Windows 10               |
| `2025`, `2022` Windows Server | 7.6, 6.0 GB | server editions                                       |

`bxcachy vm versions windows` shows all 25 (down to Windows 95 and ReactOS). In a script, pass `--version=VALUE`.

Windows installs itself the first time it starts: it downloads the ISO inside the container (3 to 8 GB) and takes a while. Watch it with `bxcachy vm open NAME --web`. When it is ready, `bxcachy vm open NAME` opens it with FreeRDP, with the clipboard shared and the window resizable. **You need your own Windows license.** The install uses generic trial keys that do not activate Windows.

Windows needs `/dev/kvm`: turn on virtualization in the firmware and put yourself in the `kvm` group. `vm doctor` tells you what is missing. Defaults: half your RAM (4 to 8 GB), half your cores, a 64 GB disk. Change them with `--ram`, `--cpus` and `--disk`.

## Where everything is

|           What            |                                                    Where                                                     |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Disk and files of each VM | `~/.local/share/bxcachy/vms/NAME` (`storage` for Windows, `config` for Linux)                                |
| The VM's record           | `~/.config/bxcachy/vms/NAME.json`                                                                            |
| Its password              | your keyring, as `BXCACHY_VM_NAME_PASSWORD` (see `bxcachy secrets`)                                          |
| Shared folder             | `~/Windows` (drive Z: in Windows) or `~/Shared` (inside the Linux desktop); `--share=PATH` or `--share=none` |
| App menu entry            | `~/.local/share/applications/bxcachy-vm-NAME.desktop`                                                        |
| The container images      | in Podman or Docker (`podman image ls`)                                                                      |

`bxcachy vm size` shows how much disk each VM uses. Everything listens on `127.0.0.1` only.

## Stop, remove

```bash
bxcachy vm stop dev
bxcachy vm remove dev            # the container, its data, password and menu entry (it asks first)
bxcachy vm remove dev --keep-data
```

Your shared folder is never deleted.

Exporting keys globally is opt-in. Move keys between machines with bxcachy secrets export (encrypted with age). Local models bxcachy ai models list|ps|pull MODEL|rm|enable drives Ollama. bxcachy gpu doctor shows what your GPU needs ( ollama-cuda or ollama-rocm ). Skills for every agent Skills are small SKILL.md files that teach an agent how to do one thing well. BxCachy stores them once in ~/.agents/skills and links each one into the skills folder of every agent you have (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode). A skill that failed its audit is refused. Skills are optional in the wizard (AI page).
markdown:
# AI agents and skills

## Agents

BxCachy installs and launches coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) and orchestrators.

```bash
bxcachy ai list
bxcachy ai default claude-code --yes
bxcachy ai launch                   # the default agent, with its keys loaded
bxcachy ai shell                    # a pull-down terminal (Super+`)
bxcachy ai session start            # a persistent tmux session
```

## API keys

Keys are stored in your desktop keyring (BxCachy installs one if you have none), never in files or shell history.

```bash
bxcachy secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY     # typed hidden
bxcachy secrets list
bxcachy secrets run ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -- some-command
```

Each key is marked as an AI key or another kind, and agents declare which providers they accept (OpenCode can use several). Exporting keys globally is opt-in. Move keys between machines with `bxcachy secrets export` (encrypted with age).

## Local models

`bxcachy ai models list|ps|pull MODEL|rm|enable` drives Ollama. `bxcachy gpu doctor` shows what your GPU needs (`ollama-cuda` or `ollama-rocm`).

## Skills for every agent

**Skills** are small `SKILL.md` files that teach an agent how to do one thing well. BxCachy stores them once in `~/.agents/skills` and links each one into the skills folder of every agent you have (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode). A folder of your own with the same name is never replaced.

```bash
bxcachy skills install bxcachy boxlang matchbox --yes
bxcachy skills status
bxcachy skills search matchbox            # the skills.boxlang.io hub
bxcachy skills install ortus-boxlang/skills/boxlang-developer~language-fundamentals --yes
bxcachy skills update --yes
```

|    Name    |                          What it is                          |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bxcachy`  | Five skills about BxCachy itself, shipped inside the program |
| `boxlang`  | BoxLang language fundamentals, from the hub                  |
| `matchbox` | The MatchBox runtime, from the hub                           |

The hub ([skills.boxlang.io](https://skills.boxlang.io)) audits every skill. A skill that failed its audit is refused. Skills are optional in the wizard (AI page).

# BoxLang and MatchBox

The installer puts in Java 21, **bvm** (BoxLang Version Manager), **mvm** (MatchBox Version Manager), BoxLang and MatchBox. `bxcachy boxlang` sits on top of them.

```bash
bxcachy boxlang status
bxcachy boxlang use latest              # bvm: install if missing, then use
bxcachy boxlang use snapshot
bxcachy boxlang matchbox use latest     # mvm
bxcachy boxlang modules list            # the live ForgeBox list
bxcachy boxlang modules search ai
bxcachy boxlang modules install bx-ai bx-sites
bxcachy boxlang modules update
bxcachy boxlang vscode                  # the BoxLang extension and developer pack
bxcachy boxlang links                   # docs and sites
bxcachy boxlang welcome                 # a getting-started page
```

Modules come from [ForgeBox](https://forgebox.io) and install with `bx-module`. VS Code is a default app; the wizard offers to add the BoxLang extension (`ortus-solutions.vscode-boxlang`) and the developer pack.

## Compile to a native binary

```bash
matchbox script.bxs
```

[MatchBox](https://matchbox.boxlang.io) compiles BoxLang to bytecode on a Rust runtime and can build standalone native binaries. BxCachy itself is built this way.

## Links

[Try BoxLang](https://try.boxlang.io) · [Docs](https://boxlang.ortusbooks.com) · [BoxLang AI](https://ai.boxlang.io) · [BoxLang Agents](https://bxagents.ai) · [BoxLang Sites](https://bxsites.io) · [ForgeBox](https://forgebox.io) · [Skills](https://skills.boxlang.io)

markdown:
# Updates and channels

## Channels

| Channel  |                        What it is                         |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `stable` | Tagged releases                                           |
| `beta`   | The bleeding edge: a build of every push to `development` |

```bash
bxcachy update channel            # show
bxcachy update channel beta       # switch
```

Both are also in the control center (Settings → Updates).

## Update BxCachy

```bash
bxcachy update check              # exit 10 means an update is available
bxcachy update apply --yes        # download, verify, replace atomically
```

The release information is signed (Ed25519) and the binary's SHA-256 is checked against it; a bad signature or checksum changes nothing.

## Get told about updates

```bash
bxcachy update notifications on     # a daily user timer shows a desktop notification
bxcachy update notifications off
```

The notification covers BxCachy and pending system packages.

## Update the system

```bash
bxcachy system update --yes       # snapshot first (snapper or timeshift), then pacman -Syu and yay -Sua
```

## Agent skills

`bxcachy skills update --yes` refreshes the skills BxCachy installed.

markdown:
# Move to another machine

```bash
bxcachy settings export my-settings.tar.gz
bxcachy settings import my-settings.tar.gz --yes
```

Export bundles `~/.config/bxcachy` (answers, shortcuts, runner and update settings) **without secrets, backups or state** . Import backs up each existing file as `NAME.bak-STAMP` first and refuses archives with paths outside `bxcachy/`.

Keys travel separately and encrypted: `bxcachy secrets export` and `bxcachy secrets import`.

To set up a new machine without touching the old one, export only the wizard answers: `bxcachy init --export answers.json`, then on the new machine `bxcachy init --from answers.json`, or run unattended with `--answers answers.json --yes`.

title: Security
body: Security Releases are signed. CI signs each channel's version-latest.properties and install.sh with an Ed25519 key. The public key is built into the program and into the published installer. The installer and bxcachy update verify the signature and the SHA-256 of every file they download; any mismatch stops before anything changes. The first curl | bash trusts the script it downloads (TLS and the bucket). For a stricter first install, download install.sh and install.sh.sig and check the signature yourself with keys/release.pub . Nothing runs without a plan. Commands that change the system print a plan and need --yes . Your files are yours. BxCachy keeps a config you changed and only rewrites files it wrote; every write is atomic, backed up and journaled. Secrets live in the desktop keyring (or a private file fallback), are typed hidden, and never appear in answers files, logs or shell history. Skills from the hub are audited; one that failed its audit is refused. Fingerprint, security key, SSH and passwordless sudo bxcachy security can turn on a fingerprint or a security key for sudo , the SSH server and passwordless sudo. These touch PAM and sudoers, so they are guarded. bxcachy security status bxcachy security fingerprint on --dry-run # prints the exact PAM line first bxcachy security fingerprint on --yes bxcachy security fingerprint enroll --yes bxcachy security fido2 register --yes # touch the key; `fido2 on` refuses until one is registered bxcachy security fido2 on --yes bxcachy security ssh-server on --yes bxcachy security passwordless-sudo on --yes Only /etc/pam.d/sudo is changed , never the login, the login screen or the lock screen. The line is auth sufficient , so your password still works when the reader or key is missing. The first time, the original is kept as /etc/pam.d/sudo.bxcachy-backup ; off removes exactly the line BxCachy added. sudoers is checked with visudo -cf before the file is installed, so a mistake cannot lock sudo out.
